title: Sound the Alarm for Democracy

location.venue: Vigo County Annex Building of Terre Haute

description:
***If you are not from Terre Haute, Please start one of these near you! We would love this to be Nationwide!!!***

The Trump Administration and Elon Musk are acting with selfishness, hiding their actions in cowardice, and systematically dismantling the values upon which our country was built. The speed of the destruction has been truly horrific, and we the people are alarmed at the state of our democracy! So Indivisible Wabash Valley has launched the "Sound the Alarm for Democracy" weekly event. 

Every Monday at 12:05 pm, sound the panic on your car alarms, honk your horns, bang a drum, blow a trumpet, sing the Star Spangled Banner, or make noise however you can. The idea is that anyone can participate, no matter where they are, no matter what they are doing.

Those who are able will meet at the Vigo County Annex each week, everyone else, just make noise wherever you are: homes, schools, churches, jobs! We want to let our neighbors, our elected officials, and the rest of the world know that a lot of us are out here, still standing together to protect our democracy, and the rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, fought for and defended for 250 years and counting.

JOIN US EVERY MONDAY!!
SOUND THE ALARM FOR DEMOCRACY

title: We The People Wednesdays in Walnut Creek
description:
This is a local Indivisible event organized by Indivisible ReSisters Contra Costa!  Join us every Wednesday evening from 5-6 p.m. at the corner of Ygnacio Valley Road and Civic Drive for a rousing honk and wave visibility action.  Bring your signs and raise your voice for democracy and to protect our rights!  

This is a nonviolent event. Stay within your rights, don’t break laws, stay safe, stay peaceful, and avoid any risk you don’t feel comfortable with. Don’t obstruct traffic, impede pedestrians, or commit any acts of property damage. If counterprotestors appear, do your best to ignore them.  When people shout from cars, just remember that we are standing for their rights, too.  They just don't know it.

This is a busy intersection and cars drive fast.  Please stay on the sidewalk at least a few feet from cars.  We can spread out down the block and take a stand on the pedestrian overpass.  Safety is our top priority.  If you have any concerns during this event, please find a peace ambassador in an orange vest and they will help.

There are several parking lots within walking distance or you can find street parking at Civic Park or on Civic Drive or Arroyo Way.

title: March for Good Trouble - Democracy Action Network / Indivisible
description:
# March for Good Trouble
## Cast off the chains of Tyranny

**Saturday, July 19th | 11:00 AM - 2:00 PM**

Join us for a powerful day of "Good Trouble" as we march for democracy, human rights, and the foundational principles that make America truly America. In the spirit of John Lewis and the great civil rights leaders who came before us, we gather to peacefully resist tyranny and stand up for our rights.

## "We Hold These Truths to Be Self-Evident"

This march honors the revolutionary spirit of our Declaration of Independence—a document born from resistance against tyranny. Today, we carry forward that same courage, declaring that **silence equals tyranny** and that we must actively defend the democracy we inherited.

## March Route & Activities

**The Journey:** We'll march together to Plummer Park and back—approximately 4.5 miles of solidarity, song, and shared purpose.

**Resistance Faire Activities:**
- **Protest Songs & Les Misérables Performances** - Lift your voice in songs of resistance and hope
- **Declaration of Independence Recitation** - Hear the words that sparked a revolution
- **Video Booth** - Share your story and commitment to democracy
- **Civil Rights Movement Photo Exhibition** - Honor those who paved the way
- **Resistance Pledge Ceremony** - Make your commitment to continued action
- **Additional Activities at Plummer Park** - Community building and connection

## Our Call to Action

We want America to be America—a nation where all people are truly created equal, where tyranny cannot take root, and where good trouble creates lasting change. This march is our collective stand against government repression and our commitment to:

- **Fighting for Freedom** in all its forms
- **Defeating Modern Tyranny** through peaceful resistance
- **Defending Human Rights** for every person
- **Supporting the Cause** of justice and equality
- **Casting Off the Chains** of oppression wherever they exist

## Join the Movement

Whether you've been fighting for decades or this is your first act of resistance, you belong here. Bring your voice, your energy, and your commitment to good trouble. Together, we'll march not just through our neighborhoods, but toward a more perfect union.

*Comfortable walking shoes recommended. Water and snacks provided. All peaceful participants welcome.*

**Stand up. March on. Make good trouble.**

title: Protest Elon Musk's Illegal Government Takeover #TeslaTakedown - Stanford Saturdays
description:
PLEASE READ COMPLETELY before attending!

This is a peaceful, nonviolent protest on the sidewalk in front of the Stanford Tesla showroom. There will be theatrics and dancing. Get ready to improv! We'll also be looping through Stanford Shopping Mall with peaceful positive energy. Of course you may opt out and continue to demonstrate in front of the Tesla showroom. 

We know making lots of noise is typically part of a good protest. But most protests aren’t right across the street from a Ronald McDonald House. Let’s take care to keep our noise levels down to a dull roar. Bring your energy and spirit, but let’s refrain from the cowbells, drums and car honks. We can get our point across without interfering with our neighbors on the other side of the road.

Wear your favorite wig, big hat, or costume. We want to have fun and to feel like a party during our demonstrations! Signs, flags, and similar items are welcome.

This is a peaceful demonstration, and any conflicts or altercations will not be tolerated. Walk away if one arises and report it to the demonstration leader on site if it is a serious altercation. We will comply with requests from the police and mall security, including if we are asked to leave. By the way, we have already have a fantastic relationship with mall security, which is a plus!

Do not boo or confront Tesla drivers or cars, or Tesla employees. Remember that most Tesla drivers are our allies, and many are protesting with us!

Please Note: Photos may be taken and published at this event, including by attendees and professional photographers. If you prefer not to have your image captured or shared, please take your own precautions (e.g., wear a mask, hat, or wig).

#BoycottTesla #DivestFromTesla

title: Wheeler Salmonberry Trail Ground Building
description:
**Join The Salmonberry Trail in our exciting ground breaking event at Waterfront Park in Wheeler!**

The City of Wheeler is excited to announce that we are taking the first steps toward revitalization of Wheeler’s section of the Salmonberry Trail through partnership with the Salmonberry Trail Foundation and Tillamook Coast Visitors Association. We will be holding a **Ground Building event and ceremony on July 12, 2025 from 1:00-5:00 PM.** We truly could not be more excited for the recreational opportunities this trail will provide for our community.

This transformative project holds the potential to deliver lasting, meaningful benefits to our community. By linking the Willamette Valley to the Coast, it will not only strengthen regional connectivity but also invigorate rural tourism and empower small businesses. It champions public health and safe, active transportation options while expanding equitable access to the outdoors for all residents. Most importantly, it lays the foundation for sustainable infrastructure that will support our economy, environment, and quality of life for generations to come.

We will have local vendors, music, games, and a ribbon cutting ceremony celebrating the beginning of this coastal section of the trail. 
- July 12th, 1PM - 5PM
- Waterfront Park (500 Marine Dr, Wheeler, OR 97147)

---
**ABOUT THE SALMONBERRY TRAIL**
The Salmonberry Trail is an 82-mile multi-use path transforming a historic rail line into Oregon’s next big adventure. Connecting communities from the Willamette Valley to the coast, the trail will provide safe routes for recreation and education, expand economic opportunities, and improve public health. In partnership with local organizations, it will offer unique educational programs while promoting outdoor activity and conservation, making it a cornerstone of community development and environmental stewardship across the state.

**Wheeler Demonstration Project – Salmonberry Trail**
The Wheeler Demonstration Project is a short, high-impact segment of the Salmonberry Trail located in downtown Wheeler. This 1,800-foot trail segment runs north from Rector Street, across Hemlock Street, and along the bay side of the Oregon Coast Scenic Railway tracks adjacent to Botts Marsh. It features a compacted gravel path for pedestrians, designed to enhance safety and encourage walking in the downtown area.
Developed in partnership with the City of Wheeler, Oregon Coast Scenic Railway, Lower Nehalem Community Trust, and the Salmonberry Trail Foundation, the project supports local economic activity, offers environmental education through interpretive signage, and provides a model for similar efforts in other communities along the trail corridor.

title: ¡Alto a Avelo, Acabemos con ICE! Lakeland, FL

address_lines: Harden Blvd y Town Center Dr

description:
# 🦅 Defendamos la Constitución 🛑 Alto a Avelo ⛓️‍💥 Acabemos con ICE 🧊
*Organizado por DESFINANCIAR A LA OLIGARQUÍA · BENDICIÓN DE LA LIBERTAD · INDIVISIBLES*
[in English](https://mobilize.us/s/3PHiaS)

### Demostración Pública No Partidista — Sábado, 28 de junio de 2025
#### Lakeland, Florida

# 📢 ESTO NO ES TU TÍPICO EVENTO DE LIBERTAD DE EXPRESIÓN
#### Asegúrate de leer todas las instrucciones

Nos estamos levantando contra el contrato de 150 millones de dólares entre Avelo Airlines y ICE (la agencia de migración de EE.UU.) para operar vuelos de deportación. Estos vuelos están facilitando la expulsión de personas sin el debido proceso legal — lo que va en contra de los principios fundamentales de la república.

Este es un llamado urgente a la acción. Nos estamos organizando para exigir que Avelo cancele su contrato con ICE y deje de participar en deportaciones inconstitucionales.

# 🪧 Nuestras demandas
✈️ Avelo Airlines: Terminen su contrato con ICE — ahora.

Es ICE o nosotros.

No se puede servir al pueblo y al mismo tiempo a una agencia que separa familias, priva de alimentos a personas, niega acceso al agua, atención médica, causa muertes, impone condiciones de esclavitud, realiza esterilizaciones sin consentimiento y se niega a reconocer certificados de nacimiento estadounidenses ni identificaciones oficiales.

Si eligen a ICE, cancelaremos sus subsidios públicos y el apoyo financiado por los contribuyentes.

✊ Residentes del Condado de Polk: Boicoteen a ICE y a cualquier empresa que se beneficie de sus actividades.

✊ Ciudad de Lakeland: Dejen de otorgar a Avelo $30,000 anuales en incentivos de mercadeo.

✊ Condado de Polk: Cancelen el acuerdo de $6 millones en beneficios corporativos con Avelo.

✊ DHS y James Uthmeier: No a la “Alcatraz de los caimanes”. No a las jaulas en tierras sagradas.

✊ ICE: Fuera de Florida. Dejen de aterrorizar escuelas, hospitales, tribunales y lugares de trabajo. Pongan fin a la detención. Deporten solo a delincuentes violentos con condenas penales.

✊ LPD y PCSO: No cooperen con ICE. Arresten a los agentes de ICE que operen sin órdenes judiciales firmadas para casos de delitos violentos.

✊ Sheriff Grady Judd: Emita una declaración pública denunciando a ICE y comprométase a apoyar a los residentes del Condado de Polk que se enfrenten a ICE.

✊ Scott Franklin, Rick Scott, Ashley Moody: Recorten los fondos y abolan ICE.

✊ Legislatura del Estado de Florida: Prohíban el uso de dinero de los contribuyentes para operaciones de ICE. Aprueben leyes que prohíban la cooperación con ICE más allá de lo que exige la ley federal.

# 🛑 ¿POR QUÉ PROTESTAMOS?

❌ Avelo está colaborando con detenciones ilegales y deportaciones sin audiencia legal.

❌ Ciudadanos estadounidenses y personas con permisos de trabajo — como Juan Carlos López-Gómez y Heidy Sánchez Tejeda — han sido detenidos sin justificación.

❌ Hay niños que están siendo separados de sus padres, sin acceso a abogados, e incluso deportados mientras todavía están en medio de procesos legales por custodia — como el caso de una niña ciudadana estadounidense de dos años conocida como V.M.L.

❌ Se están violando nuestros derechos constitucionales: el debido proceso, el derecho a defensa legal, y la protección frente a abusos del poder ejecutivo.

# ✨ NOSOTROS DEFENDEMOS:

- A las familias
- Los derechos de las personas migrantes
- El debido proceso
- Las libertades constitucionales para todxs
- La responsabilidad de las empresas que lucran con el sufrimiento humano

# 🗓️ DETALLES DEL EVENTO

📍 Lakeland, FL (la ubicación exacta se enviará por correo después del registro)

🕒 Sábado, 28 de junio de 2025, de 5:00 p. m. a 7:00 p. m.

🎨 Habrá carteles disponibles (pero puedes traer el tuyo, sobre todo si destaca casos de personas detenidas o deportadas de forma injusta)

🎭 Bienvenidos los disfraces, los instrumentos y los niños

🌞 Vístete de acuerdo al clima. Trae bloqueador solar, gafas de sol y usa mascarilla si deseas mantener privacidad

🚶‍♀️ Caminata corta (aproximadamente 320 metros) por veredas accesibles

📢 Habrá cánticos & vamos a cantar y dejar que los carteles hablen por nosotros

🚻 Habrá baños públicos disponibles cerca

🚗 No estaciones en el aeropuerto

# 💡 RECOMENDACIONES

👍 Nuestro compromiso es con la no violencia. Este será un acto pacífico. Sé respetuoso en todo momento.

👍 Mantente alerta: pueden aparecer infiltrados o medios falsos haciéndose pasar por prensa independiente. Verifica antes de dar entrevistas.

👍 No entres en discusiones con provocadores. Algunos se hacen pasar por manifestantes.

👍 Enfócate en crear unidad y en defender nuestra república democrática y constitucional.

# 🎶 CANTEMOS POR LA LIBERTAD — Te recomendamos practicar estas canciones:

[This Land is Your Land](https://youtu.be/2Q7PULELvok?si=2ZBVKeoM5Ker0Zad)

[My Country ’Tis of Thee](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xnH_OIgNgSY)

[America the Beautiful](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWJF1yE3Y1E)

[Star Spangled Banner](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fF01L85TYaw)

# 🔗 CONFIRMA TU ASISTENCIA Y OBTÉN MÁS INFORMACIÓN

✅ Confirmar tu asistencia en Mobilize es opcional

🌐 También publicaremos la información del evento en: www.blessedbyliberty.org

📄 Para más información sobre el contrato entre Avelo y ICE: www.stopavelo.org

Nos mantenemos firmes — y unidos, vamos a vencer.

#DesfinanciarLaOligarquía #DebidoProcesoParaTodxs #AltoAvelo #BendiciónDeLaLibertad #IndivisibleLakeland #Indivisible #DefiendeLaConstitución #ContraTodosLosEnemigos

title: STOP AVELO - National Day of Action | Burbank Airport, CA - iCA27
description:
STOP AVELO National Day of Action – JUNE 29, JULY 27, AUG 24 and SEPT 28 | 4 PM– 6PM

Hosted by Indivisible CA27 and Nancy Klein | Organized by STOPAVELO.ORG National

Join us as we rise up to demand justice, accountability, and human rights! 

Avelo Airlines has accepted a $150 million contract with ICE to carry out deportation flights that violate constitutional rights. These flights tear families apart and deny people their legal right to due process — a right reaffirmed by the U.S. Supreme Court. This is a cruel, inhumane, and illegal partnership, and we’re coming together across the country to stop it.

On the last Sunday of Every Month, we’re joining forces with STOPAVELO.ORG National and Defend and Resist, to protest in cities across the U.S. This is a call to action for anyone who believes in democracy, human rights, and the rule of law.  

Together, we will:

Protest at Avelo-serviced airports nationwide

Boycott Avelo Airlines and push ticket sales to zero

Demand city and state officials cancel all Avelo contracts and subsidies

Shine a spotlight on this airline’s shameful role in aiding unlawful deportations

Join us at the airport protest. Your voice counts — and it’s needed now more than ever.

Let’s stand together against fascism, family separation, and corporate complicity.
No more silence. No more flights. #StopAvelo

#PeopleOverProfit #NoICEFlights #DueProcessForAll #IndivisibleCA27
#StopAvelo #DefendandResist

These protests will be in cooperation with larger national groups doing the same actions on those weekends. We want to make very clear to drivers what we are protesting about, so please make your signs, and other messaging specific to Avelo Airlines, civil rights, due process, etc.


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*


Special thanks to STOPAVELO.ORG for choosing Indivisible CA27 as a local partner in this national campaign for justice.  Information on www.indivisibleca27.com

title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ ICE/U.S. Immigration Court in Phoenix
description:
Big events with thousands of people are great. But we also need local, more frequent rallies that show locals that they're not alone in this fight.

**When we realized the ICE was abducting people appearing at U.S. Immigration Court, we decided it would be the perfect place for an ICE-specific RhRR!**

Every Tuesday @ 7:30 am, we'll gather on the south west corner where 7th Ave, Van Buren, and Grand meet, right in front of the Social Security Administration office, which also serves as U.S. Immigration Court.

**STAY ON THE SIDEWALK**! It's public property and we've a right to be there. Be sure you **DO NOT BLOCK** access to the building—that means cars as well as people.

**Please make ICE-specific signs**, as we're here to show the busy morning commuters that they are not alone, the ICE agents that We The People care about due process for everyone, and those before the court that we support them. Because no human is illegal.

Spread the word. Come join us. All the details you need are at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

title: Democracy Rush Hour Rally: 8am Every Tuesday at University/Farley
description:
Every Tuesday, citizens have been reaching commuters on University Ave in Madison, WI with pro-democracy messages and a targeted theme each week. During morning rush hour hundreds of commuters have to sit at this red light and look at our signs! This is an opportunity to pierce through our current news (and disinformation) ecosystems with concise pro-democracy ideas, messages, and calls to action.

In your confirmation email, you will receive a link to a google doc and my email so you can get the weekly topic. For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:
General Visibility Rules:
•	Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
•	"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
•	Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:
•	Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
•	Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
•	High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
o	Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
o	Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
o	Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
•	Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
•	Material and Construction:
o	Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
o	Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
o	Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
•	Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
•	Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Weekly (Fri) Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
description:
Wow! What a great location for a standout! On 5/30, around 17 people, including a bagpiper!  What a blast! LOTS of engagement with motorists!

There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all! 

We'll have letterboards prepared for the lower part of the overpass fencing - the photo shows how that will look to folks passing on the Mass Pike. We're interacting with motorists on the Mass Pike, and on Southampton Road. We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 1/2 hours.

### How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass. 

### Parking

We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and it seems that parking would be OK there.

It looks like The Wealth Technology Group has vacated their office at 130 Southampton Rd, but the internet says that other businesses are located there, so please be mindful if you decide to park there.

### Etiquette!

We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too. 

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

title: JOHN LEWIS DAY OF ACTION - GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON in Williamsburg, VA
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

This event is being co-hosted by the League of Women Voters of the Williamsburg Area.

Our rights are under attack. Our democracy is under siege. We’ve been here before, and we know what to do.

On Thursday, July 17, we honor the anniversary of the passing of civil rights hero John Lewis, not with ceremonies, but with action at the Williamsburg James City County Courthouse, located at 5201 Monticello Avenue, Williamsburg, Va from 6pm-7:30pm. Across the country, we will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all. Join us to hear our speakers, Charles S. Gates, Community Coordination Committee Chair with YJCW NAACP and Laura F. Tripp, Vice President of the League of Women Voters of the Williamsburg Area. 

Bring a water bottle, a sign, a chair if needed, dress for the weather, and reach out if you have any questions. And spread the word!

Please note: a core principle behind our John Lewis Good Trouble Day actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. 

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. It is a continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

COMMUNITY NORMS:

Please read before attending one of our events.

One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day”.

At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept.

Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!

As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers. At larger events, these organizers will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts with yellow safety vests. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

title: Honk & Wave: Tell Avelo Airlines to Cancel ICE Agreement

address_lines: near the intersection of Rt. 13 and School Lane

description:
Co-hosted by 302 United and Indivisible Highlands and Beyond.

Avelo Airlines has accepted a $150 million contract to operate deportation flights, aiding and colluding with the federal government in the illegal removal of individuals without their right to a fair hearing or due process. 

We demand that Avelo Airlines cancels their agreement with ICE immediately. Come out and help us keep up the pressure on AVELO and to promote a boycott until they change course.

Bring signs! We will have some to share, but we urge you to continue making your own great/creative signs! (Given often fast-moving traffic, a reminder about signs: 
Keep the message simple;
use large letters;
and make the letters thick and bold.)

We'll rally on both sides of Rt. 13, so stay on whichever side of the highway you park on. Please do NOT cross the busy highway!

After the Honk & Wave, all are welcome to gather at the IHOP across the street for "Protest and Pancakes!" (You don't have to get pancakes; they have avocado toast and veggie sausage, too!) Join us to connect and converse!!

Parking Options:

Go to Lot D, $7.00 per car, then walk to the nearby sidewalk along the DuPont Hwy. (The first section of Lot D is a quick right turn after passing the ChristianaCare-GoHealth Urgent Care, right next to the Wilmington Airport.The second section of Lot D is a right turn immediately after you past this first turn for lot D.  There is a sign for Lot D at this turn.)

You can create an account online ahead of time so you can complete your payment from home in advance.  We recommend taking this step ahead of time, so you can just park and join us. Go to this link to set up your parking account: https://p-123.com/. Click on the ‘create your account now’ button. You will be asked for the zone ID which is 10500. You will add your license plate number, then pay with a credit card. 
You could also use this same link or a QR code once you arrive to pay.  The signs in the parking lot have this info.
At this link below you can see where Lot D (or Remote lot) is located:
https://www.flyilg.com/parking-wilmington-airport-ilg

Parking is also available behind the IHOP across the street: specifically, try the large shopping area lot between IHOP and Planet Fitness. (Again, if you park there, stay on that side of the road to rally along DuPont Hwy in front of the IHOP. Do NOT cross DuPont Hwy.)

description:
We're taking the lawless NC legislature to court for rigging voting maps against the people of North Carolina — a scheme that unjustly comes at the expense of Black voters, especially. It's time to sound the alarm. Are you with us?

Our federal trial against gerrymandered maps continues on Friday, June 20, at the federal courthouse in Winston-Salem, and we're calling on YOU to join us in packing the court. We're expecting key testimony!

RSVP today to join us, We'll share more details about what to expect once you sign up!

*Please note: the schedules and timing of federal trials are subject to change. We'll keep you up-to-date every step of the way!

Federal Courthouse Etiquette:
Courtroom Etiquette:
• Be punctual! Arrive on time and account for the security check in at the entrance.
o All persons are required to show a valid U.S. government issued identification
card (federal or state). The identification must show, at minimum, a person’s
photo, name, and date of birth.
o REAL ID is NOT required. The REAL ID Act takes effect on May 7, 2025. However,
the Act does NOT apply to entry to federal courthouses, which is a
constitutionally protected activity. Although a picture identification must still be
shown to court security officers, it does not need to be a REAL ID-compliant
drivers license or identification card.
• No food, beverages, or chewing gum are permitted inside the courtrooms.
• Cell phones and electronic devices are PROHIBITED in the courthouse. You must leave
them in your car.
• While in the courtroom, and particularly when the court is in session, you must remain
silent.
• Courtroom-appropriate attire is expected when present in a courtroom. Hats and
sunglasses, unless for religious or medical reasons, should be removed before entering
the courtroom.
• Please stand when the judge enters and exits the courtroom.
• No smoking is allowed in the courthouse.
• Please do not speak to attorneys for the State Board of Election or to any of the
defendants.

Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

title: Weekly (Tues) I-91 Overpass Standout - Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Bring a friend!!!

Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee visited twice in the three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue. We haven't seen him lately, but...

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

title: Celebrate Your Independence: Rally & March
description:
Celebrate Your Independence: Rally & March

Worcester City Hall (Front) | 12–2 PM | Friday, July 4, 2025

Worcester Indivisible invites you to celebrate independence YOUR way with us on the 4th of July from 12:00PM-2:00PM, at Worcester City Hall on the very spot the Declaration of Independence was first read in New England. 

DECLARE YOUR TRUTHS TO BE SELF EVIDENT. 

Whether your version of freedom and independence revolves around women’s reproductive rights, LGBTQ+ equality, ICE and immigration, Indigenous and First People rights to tribal land and sovereignty, food insecurity, housing affordability, or racial justice and equality for all, these are the fundamental principles the Declaration of Independence and the 4th of July are built on. Ignored, dismissed and unlawfully obstructed by the current Trump administration, it is to you, the people of these United States, that we must look to in order to make us whole and declare our sovereignty as a united people. 

WE THE PEOPLE DECLARE OUR INDEPENDENCE. 

Please join us for a day of declaration, celebrating our freedom of diversity and independence from a tyrannical administration by asserting the fundamental rights granted to us by both the Declaration of Independence and the United States Constitution. Let us declare our truths and rights to be self evident by making our voices heard and coming together as the diverse and united community we are, can and should be. Come with your families, wear your best 4th finery or regalia celebrating your individual expressions of independence, to enjoy good food from local food trucks, inspirational speakers, music, and tables with resources!

title: Hold Buddy Accountable
description:
This a local, recurring Indivisible event in solidarity with Brunswick, GA groups who have a standing picket in front of Buddy Carter's office there.

We meet on Wednesdays (10 a.m. OR 3:15 p.m., or both!) at the corner of Jackson Blvd. and Abercorn St. in Savannah, GA to hold Rep. Buddy Carter accountable for his actions.

As a self-proclaimed "MAGA Warrior," Carter has fought to take over Greenland; add to the deficit on higher taxes to the poorest; build more ICE detention centers (including the largest in the U.S. right in our district); cut life-saving services (like Medicaid and SNAP benefits); eliminate the child tax credit for many, especially immigrants; add out-of-pocket insurance costs in the Affordable Care Act; and try to enable the president to defy court orders (some sources: https://buddycarter.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=15398; https://prospect.org/blogs-and-newsletters/tap/2025-05-23-ten-sneaky-sleeper-provisions-trumps-big-beautiful-bill/). 

He wants to impeach lawfully acting judges and codify the damaging DOGE cuts (https://thecurrentga.org/today-from-the-current/open-records-legal-fight-in-savannah/; https://buddycarter.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=15284).

This man also wants to be our senator. Let's not let him nor the people forget the damaging actions and stances he takes.

At the start or conclusion of the picket, be sure to go into Rep. Carter's office to speak your mind and sign your name.

title: SAN MATEO - Protest for Our Democracy
description:
Indivisible San Mateo is a group of activists from the San Mateo area who are inspired by Indivisible 2.0’s call-to-action to use our local constituent power to help in the nationwide fight against Trump’s agenda.

We are committed to achieving Indivisible’s three goals of stopping Project 2025; playing hardball; and, protecting and winning elections in order to achieve the overarching goal of winning a pro-democracy House of Representatives in 2026 and ultimately defeating the Trump/MAGA/oligarch regime.

Join us in front of Ana Furniture at 3011 S El Camino and across the street in front of the West Elm store at Hillsdale Mall in San Mateo from 1 to 2:30 p.m. on Saturdays to protest the Trump regime’s destruction of our democracy.

This is a peaceful, law-abiding, non-violent action to raise awareness about the damage the Trump regime is doing to our country.

Bring your signs, your costumes and, if you have them, your drums, cowbells, whistles, saxophones, tubas, tambourines and any other musical instruments to help add to the fun! On No Kings day a bagpipe player joined us too!

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

Our Saturday actions are co-sponsored with Peace Action of San Mateo County.

title: No Kings Declaration Reading
description:
Join the Bexar County Democratic Party and Tell that Sh*t! as we host a reading of the Declaration of Independence, Bill of Rights and the Preamble. We've also got slam poets who'll be spitting some poems on what these documents mean.  We'll have voter registrars onsite.

Our nation was founded on a radical idea - that our government is by and for the people.  This promise is a contract - a social contract - that means the government works for us.  We the People. This evening will remind everyone what that contract is as we head into our 250th anniversary as a nation.

Join us on July 5th from 7-9pm at Tandem Coffeehouse, 310 Riverside Drive.

title: Leaving MAGA: Budget Cuts will not Heal
description:
The Big Ugly Bill will add 3.8 trillion to the national debt while stripping many Americans of their earned benefits like Medicaid. Cuts to benefits never heal! United we stand.

title: Small Town, Loud Voices - El Segundo
description:
This a local Indivisible event organized by El Segundo residents to stand in solidarity with our communities and stand up to the Trump administration.

This will be a family-friendly, dog-friendly, non-violent, no-vandalism, community event. We'll be staying on the grassy areas and out of the roads. Please keep it friendly, and if there is any negativity or counter-protestors, don't engage. We'll have folks on hand who can help de-escalate any situation if necessary.

What this event is:

* This is a stationary, “honk and wave” visibility event at a location that sees a lot of weekend traffic.

* This is a positive, peaceful, community-focused, and family- and dog-friendly event.

What this event is not:

* This is not a march, and there is no programming/planned speaker.

* This is not a civil disobedience event. We will not block roads, sidewalks, or the entrances of any buildings.

* We will not be engaging with any hecklers. The El Segundo Police Department is aware of the event and available to help assist to keep everyone safe if there are counter-protestors.

There are many other Indivisible events across LA, so if this doesn't sound like what you're looking for, please feel free to attend a different event.

Details:

* 10 AM to 12 PM

* Grassy area in front of the El Segundo sign at the corner of Main & Imperial in El Segundo. We will expand to the grassy area across Main if necessary.

* There is street parking along Imperial Avenue (not Imperial Highway) within El Segundo, as well as on the surrounding streets south of Imperial Ave.

* Please do not park illegally (i.e. blocking driveways or in the local businesses’ lots). We want to bring people in to our movement, not turn them off!

We can't wait to see you. We are looking forward to making our voices heard together!

Event Campaign
Good Trouble Lives On: National Day of Action

*********
SIGN UP FOR March for Good Trouble AT https://www.mobilize.us/indivisible/event/806379/
 
Cast off the chains of Tyranny
Saturday, July 19th | 11:00 AM - 2:00 PM

Join us for a powerful day of "Good Trouble" as we march for democracy, human rights, and the foundational principles that make America truly America. In the spirit of John Lewis and the great civil rights leaders who came before us, we gather to peacefully resist tyranny and stand up for our rights.

"We Hold These Truths to Be Self-Evident"
This march honors the revolutionary spirit of our Declaration of Independence—a document born from resistance against tyranny. Today, we carry forward that same courage, declaring that silence equals tyranny and that we must actively defend the democracy we inherited.

March Route & Activities
The Journey: We'll march together to Plummer Park and back—approximately 4.5 miles of solidarity, song, and shared purpose.

Resistance Faire Activities: - Protest Songs & Les Misérables Performances - Lift your voice in songs of resistance and hope - Declaration of Independence Recitation - Hear the words that sparked a revolution - Video Booth - Share your story and commitment to democracy - Civil Rights Movement Photo Exhibition - Honor those who paved the way - Resistance Pledge Ceremony - Make your commitment to continued action - Additional Activities at Plummer Park - Community building and connection

Our Call to Action
We want America to be America—a nation where all people are truly created equal, where tyranny cannot take root, and where good trouble creates lasting change. This march is our collective stand against government repression and our commitment to:

Fighting for Freedom in all its forms
Defeating Modern Tyranny through peaceful resistance
Defending Human Rights for every person
Supporting the Cause of justice and equality
Casting Off the Chains of oppression wherever they exist
Join the Movement
Whether you've been fighting for decades or this is your first act of resistance, you belong here. Bring your voice, your energy, and your commitment to good trouble. Together, we'll march not just through our neighborhoods, but toward a more perfect union.

Comfortable walking shoes recommended. Water and snacks provided. All peaceful participants welcome.

Stand up. March on. Make good trouble.

title: LGBTQ+/ DEI & Stonewall Riots 56 Years Later Rally-Brenham Saturday, June 28th
description:
The Stonewall riots, which began on June 28, 1969, are widely considered the catalyst for the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement and the inspiration for Pride celebrations. A police raid on the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in New York City, sparked days of protests and clashes, bringing attention to the systemic discrimination and violence faced by the LGBTQ+ community. 
We will also celebrate the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in our Country. Three interconnected concepts that create fair and welcoming environments for people of all backgrounds. We MUST STAND UP & PROTECT these issues. 

These events have been wonderful and are giving people opportunities to express their dissent, meet new friends, exchange ideas and have an amazing sense of camaraderie! 

We will meet behind Taco Bell in the Walmart parking lot close to the trees. Please park in this area & walk down to our easement location in front of Taco Bell. Taco Bell has been very accommodating to our efforts. They request that no vehicles park in front of their trash area even though it is marked for parking. Please consider patronizing Taco Bell at these events. Please do not block business customer parking. Lastly, please do not leave any trash.

Stay Cool & hydrated! Some take breaks and sit in Taco Bell. We will have an ice chest with cold bandanas to cool you off! Wear hats, bring umbrellas, chairs and stay as comfortable as possible in this heat. Our mission overrides any discomfort we may encounter!

Democratic Women of Brenham

title: Good Trouble Lives On in Columbus!
description:
Save the Date! Indivisible Central Ohio and other local and national organizations are ready for the next big event: Good Trouble Lives on!

Details to come! The Statehouse is a temporary location -- be on th watch for a possible location change. 

Below is the information about the national event. 

Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of action to respond to the attacks on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration. Together, we’ll remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

Coined by civil rights leader Congressman John Lewis, "Good Trouble" is the action of coming together to take peaceful, non-violent action to challenge injustice and create meaningful change. 

The civil rights leaders of the past have shown us the power of collective action. That’s why on July 17, five years since the passing of Congressman John Lewis, communities across the country will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all.

https://actionnetwork.org/event_campaigns/muskmustfall-global-day-of-celebration?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON: Richfield Rises Up Again
description:
Richfield, along with Edina and Minneapolis neighbors, had a terrific turnout at 66th and Penn for the No Kings protest in June. On Thursday, July 17 we will stand up again at 66th and Penn to do our part to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the United States. 

"Good Trouble Lives On" is the follow-up to No Kings. Again, it will be a national day of nonviolent action to protest the attacks on civil and human rights by the Trump administration--- and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

Why July 17? The date marks the anniversary of the passing of civil rights icon and Congressman John Lewis, who admonished his supporters to make "Good Trouble" to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of activism. 

"Good Trouble Lives On" is more than a protest; it’s a moral reckoning. It is a continuation of the movement to which John Lewis dedicated his life --- and a new front in the struggle for freedom and justice for all.

This event at 66th and Penn is being organized in cooperation with Indivisible for All - Richfield, Minnesota. 

***PLEASE TAKE NOTE*** A core principle behind Good Trouble Lives On actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and views.

title: "Honk for Democracy" Chevy Chase (Brookville Rd/East-West Hwy)
description:
This is a peaceful "roadside rally" during the evening rush hour to show passing drivers that we're committed to our democracy.  
We've been doing this almost every week since March, and have learned that many drivers are genuinely grateful to see us; and participants have told us that it's boosted their morale.
It sometimes goes after 6:15 if people want to stay.
Our messaging is strictly PRO DEMOCRACY and specifically not anti-Trump. We take this approach to demonstrate a non-threatening style of protest that we hope will appeal to a wide array of observers--esp. those who may be unfamiliar with, or uncomfortable with, protests. 

This event would be a good fit for you if:
(1) You live nearby (-> you'll need little travel time, meet people from the area), 
OR
(2) You live further away but are interested in doing this kind of thing near you. (You can test the waters, & we can perhaps help you start one in your neighborhood.)
This is weather-dependent. Please register if you're interested so we can confirm with you closer to the time. (You can cancel your signup later-- we understand people's busy lives!)

Good Trouble Lives On: Greenbrier Valley is part of a national day of nonviolent action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

On July 17, the anniversary of Congressman John Lewis’s passing, we’re taking action across the country to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of Good Trouble.

From voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act to the criminalization of protest, the Trump administration is launching a full-scale attack on our civil and human rights. But we know the truth: in America, the power lies with the people, and we’re rising to prove it.

This is more than a protest; it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** A core principle behind our Good Trouble Lives On actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

title: Bigger Than Dobbs II: Stop the GOP War on Women
description:
Last year, Indivisibles warned the public about Project 2025, holding standouts and rallies with signs saying "Abortion is just the tip of the iceberg” and "Republicans are trying to turn back the clock” with antiquated laws like the Comstock Act. 

This year we are seeing the implementation of Project 2025’s regressive policies that target women. Indivisibles are sounding the alarm across Massachusetts about attacks on our rights and freedoms from voting to bodily autonomy. 

Join us on the Bedford St. sidewalk next to the Women’s Monument in Lexington Center from 1-2pm to protest the GOP’s escalating attacks on reproductive healthcare, voting rights, and other issues affecting women. This standout is co-hosted by Mystic Valley Action 4 Reproductive Justice and will be one of more than 20 others across Massachusetts.

This is a peaceful, non-violent gathering. Some signs will be provided, but feel free to bring your own!

title: Bigger Than Dobbs II: Stop Trump's War on Women
description:
Bigger Than Dobbs II: Stop Trump's and the GOP's War on Women

March Forward/Indivisible Quincy is organizing a "Bigger Than Dobbs'' rally to Stop the War on Women, Sunday 6/29 from 2-4 pm in the Hancock Adams Common outside Quincy City Hall. Speakers will include local activists, organizations, and elected officials. Some signs will be provided, but feel free to bring your own!

Our event is part of a weekend of action supported by Indivisible and the Women's March to mark the anniversary of the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision, sadly overturning the decades of case law for Roe vs Wade. In the barrage of attacks on our democracy, it is marginalized groups and women who are the targets. Despite our warnings and protests, the current Republican party, with Donald Trump at the helm, have accelerated their plan to implement Project 2025.

Their plan to restore a white, Christian patriarchy was clearly stated in Project 2025. We warned that Republicans were "turning back the clock" and that "abortion was just the tip of the iceberg."  Each section detailed how the freedoms of women would be curtailed. As we pointed out, abortion bans are just the beginning. Their aim is to put women back into traditional "Biblically-based marriages," without careers or reproductive rights or even the right to vote, and to punish those who won't abide by their rules. 

In the time since SCOTUS ruled to overturn Roe, we have seen a degradation of democracy across the board while attacks on women have been quietly happening. There aren't armed, masked men abducting women who won't comply (yet) but it’s clear - from the cancellation of medical research pertaining to women, to the firings of top female military officials, to voter suppression law specifically targeting married women, the GOP War on Women must be stopped. This is our message: Stop Trump's War on Women!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Good Trouble Lives On

address_lines: Foothill Boulevard & North Indian Hill Boulevard

description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Coined by civil rights leader Congressman John Lewis, "Good Trouble" is the action of coming together to take peaceful, non-violent action to challenge injustice and create meaningful change. 

The civil rights leaders of the past have shown us the power of collective action. That’s why on July 17, five years since the passing of Congressman John Lewis, communities across the country will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Overpasses for Democracy: Six I-91 Overpasses in VERMONT!
description:
**Stand up for democracy with your neighbors across the region! Hundreds of us will stand with banners, flags, and signs on overpasses across Massachusetts, Vermont, and Connecticut. These peaceful standouts have been immensely successful, so we are expanding them to a monthly event on the 4th Friday of each month, 3:00 pm - 6:00 pm (see list below of times for each individual overpass) rain or shine unless there is severe weather conditions. Register now to get updates and more information.**

LINK TO INTERACTIVE MAP: https://www.google.com/maps/d/edit?mid=1uNICTBrKbDlXD1V7RGMfQRw4opGgRlU&usp=sharing

**These overpass standouts are being organized by a coalition of pro-democracy groups across New England.  The below six overpass locations are being sponsored by Brattleboro Indivisible!**


* Tyler Hill Rd, I-91 overpass Vernon,VT -- Every Friday 3:30-5:00pm (3-6pm on the 4th Fridays)                                                    

* Exit 2, I-91 overpass, Brattleboro, VT - Western Ave - Please do not park or stand anywhere near the Deli -- Every Friday 3:30-5:00pm (3-6pm on the 4th Fridays)

* Black Mountain Rd, I-91 overpass, Brattleboro, VT -- Every Friday 3:30-5:00pm (3-6pm on the 4th Fridays)

* Exit 4, I-91 overpass, Putney, VT  -- Every Friday 5:00-6:00pm - Please do not arrive early and do not park in local business lots (still 5-6pm on the 4th Fridays)

* Near Santa's Land/ Route 5, I-91 overpass, Putney, VT -- Every Friday 3:30-5:00pm (3-6pm on the 4th Fridays)

* Kurn Hattin Rd, I-91 overpass, Westminster, VT -- Every Friday 3:30-5:00pm (3-6pm on the 4th Fridays)


If you believe in Demanding Due Process for All

If you believe in the Power of Free Speech and Peaceful Protest

If you believe in Remaining a Democracy instead of having a King

If you believe in Supporting your Fellow Community Members and ALL Americans impacted by current DC Policies

If you believe in Having an Efficient, Effective Government that Respects its Citizens

Voice your opposition to the threat on OUR Democracy, our Community and our Environment!

title: Bigger Than Dobbs II Overpass Standout: Show Up to Help Stop the GOP War on Women
description:
Stop Trump's War on Women!

In 2024, we warned the public that Republicans were "turning back the clock" and that "abortion was just the tip of the iceberg." Their plan was clear in Project 2025, the 900-page document outlining their white-Christian plan to restore the patriarchy. Each section detailed their plans to roll back the progress over the past several decades made for women's rights. As we pointed out, a nationwide abortion ban is just the beginning. Their aim is to put women back into traditional "Biblically-based marriages," without careers or reproductive rights or even the right to vote, and to punish those who won't abide by their rules.

It's been only three years since SCOTUS ruled to overturn Roe and in those years we have seen a degradation of democracy across the board while the attacks on women have been quietly happening. There aren't armed, masked men abducting women who won't comply - yet - but the foundation is being laid. From the cancellation of medical research pertaining to women, to the firings of top female military officials, to voter suppression law specifically targeting married women, the GOP War on Women must be stopped.

In an effort to get Americans to have more children, the Trump administration has proposed ideas such as a $5,000 “baby bonus” or a $1,000 tax-deferred investment account for children born between 2025 and 2029. It’s as if we’re suddenly in a game of Monopoly: Have a baby, pass go and collect cash!

Join us and say "NO!"  We choose to have, or not have, children for non-tax related reasons.  You can't entice us with false promises.

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON:
description:
Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of nonviolent actions in response to the attacks on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration. We have to remind them the power lies within the people.

From voter suppression bills, to the racial attacks and disappearance of profiled immigrants and even to the criminalization of protesting, the Trump administration is attacking our civil and human rights. Look for the pop-up tent to easily get registered.

Registration Pop-Up Tent: Will be located on the northeast side of the bridge, under our Flag! Come and register to vote.

Details: This is a rain or shine event. Make wind and rainproof signs. There is plenty of parking around this area. It would be great if people did not park in front on the street where we will be standing. Bring your flags too!

Coined by civil rights leader Congressman John Lewis, "Good Trouble" is the action of coming together to take peaceful, non-violent action to challenge injustice and create meaningful change.

The civil rights leaders of the past have shown us the power of collective action. That’s why on July 17, five years since the passing of Congressman John Lewis, communities across the country will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

If we know you are coming, we can have a volunteer ready to help you get situated.

title: Protest for Women's Rights!
description:
Join us Saturday, June 28th at noon at the Milestone Rotary to Protest for Women’s Rights!  Three years after the “Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization” Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade and federal constitutional protections for abortion, we won’t go back. This weekend, Indivisible groups and allies across MA are putting a spotlight on the GOP War on Women. This is bigger than Dobbs. This is no longer just about abortion, as the GOP's Project 2025 is turning back the clock on everything the women's movement and the civil rights movement has accomplished over the past half century.  We are standing up to protect women’s access to health care services like abortion and birth control, social services like Medicare and SNAP, voting rights, equal employment rights, and protecting women from abuse and violence.  The Trump administration has diminished women’s representation in federal positions and the military, removed recognition of women’s achievements, and cut funding for programs women rely on to take care of themselves and their families.  We need to urge our elected representatives to defeat the current Republican budget proposal and continue to fight illegal executive orders in the courts.

We are committed to peaceful protest and attendee safety.  Please do not cross into the center circle of the Rotary.

title: Kill the Bill Protest - 50501 Pensacola Florida
description:
"KILL THE BILL" HONK & WAVE PROTEST - CELEBRATE FREEDOM

Urgent call to come help preserve our Independence on July 5th in Pensacola, Florida at the "KILL THE BILL" Honk & Wave Protest. We must stop Trump's so called "Big Beautiful Bill" which is actually "The Big Billionaire Bill to Tyranny." Tyranny will allow for cruel and oppressive government rule over US.

This Bill will destroy our safety net programs, destroy our environmental protections, rob from the poor to give even more to the rich, expand Trump's executive powers beyond the Constitution, and destroy our hard fought liberty and representative democracy!

We the people are NOT giving our government to a King or wannabe Dictator!

A founding father, Benjamin Franklin, when asked what type of government the Constitutional Convention adopted, said, "A republic, if you can keep it." Franklin explained what a democracy is by saying, "Democracy is two wolves and a lamb voting on what to have for lunch. Liberty is a well-armed lamb contesting the vote!"

Independence Day is about the fight for freedom. The American Revolution was a stand against tyranny and kings. That same spirit has lived on—from the Boston Tea Party to the Underground Railroad, from Stonewall to the Civil Rights Movement.
Now, America is in crisis, again. Real democracy feels out of reach. Freedom is in trouble. This is our country, there are NO KINGS! ALL elected officials work for US, for the good of we, the American people! Tell our Representatives to "Kill the Bill" will increase the budget deficit and the national debt, PRIMARILY DUE TO TAX CUTS IN THE BILL WHICH OUTWEIGH SPENDING REDUCTIONS.

We invite Pensacola Patriots to come fill the four big corners of the busy intersection at 9th Av. and Airport Blvd. Saturday, July 5th, from 10 to Noon to proclaim, "KILL THE BILL." Come celebrate freedom, life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness for all by righteous DEI (diversity, equity, and inclusion) guiding principles.

title: FREE AMERICA WEEKEND
description:
CELEBRATE FREEDOM. IGNITE YOUR REBELLION

Independence Day is about the fight for freedom. The American Revolution was a stand against tyranny and kings. That same spirit has lived on—from the Boston Tea Party to the Underground Railroad, from Stonewall to the Civil Rights Movement.

America is in crisis. Real democracy feels out of reach. Freedom is in trouble.
This July 4th weekend, while the U.S. marks Independence Day, we’ll gather across the country—on porches, in town squares, backyards, and streets—to stand for real freedom and build a vision of a Free America brick by brick. 

Free America is wherever we are. Free America is whatever we make it.

THIS IS YOUR INVITATION TO TAKE IT BACK.

Your freedom. Your people. Your rebellion.

They want us scared, divided, and alone. They don’t want us to dream about freedom. But that’s exactly what we have to do.

This Fourth of July, we will be in the streets with songs of freedom and joy. The dream of American freedom belongs to all of us, and we will not stop in our pursuit of its promise, now or ever. 

Please join Yuba-Sutter Democrats as we take back our government.

title: March for Good Trouble - Democracy Action Network / Indivisible
description:
# March for Good Trouble
## Cast off the chains of Tyranny

**Saturday, July 19th | 11:00 AM - 2:00 PM**

Join us for a powerful day of "Good Trouble" as we march for democracy, human rights, and the foundational principles that make America truly America. In the spirit of John Lewis and the great civil rights leaders who came before us, we gather to peacefully resist tyranny and stand up for our rights.

## "We Hold These Truths to Be Self-Evident"

This march honors the revolutionary spirit of our Declaration of Independence—a document born from resistance against tyranny. Today, we carry forward that same courage, declaring that **silence equals tyranny** and that we must actively defend the democracy we inherited.

## March Route & Activities

**The Journey:** We'll march together to Plummer Park and back—approximately 4.5 miles of solidarity, song, and shared purpose.

**Resistance Faire Activities:**
- **Protest Songs & Les Misérables Performances** - Lift your voice in songs of resistance and hope
- **Declaration of Independence Recitation** - Hear the words that sparked a revolution
- **Video Booth** - Share your story and commitment to democracy
- **Civil Rights Movement Photo Exhibition** - Honor those who paved the way
- **Resistance Pledge Ceremony** - Make your commitment to continued action
- **Additional Activities at Plummer Park** - Community building and connection

## Our Call to Action

We want America to be America—a nation where all people are truly created equal, where tyranny cannot take root, and where good trouble creates lasting change. This march is our collective stand against government repression and our commitment to:

- **Fighting for Freedom** in all its forms
- **Defeating Modern Tyranny** through peaceful resistance
- **Defending Human Rights** for every person
- **Supporting the Cause** of justice and equality
- **Casting Off the Chains** of oppression wherever they exist

## Join the Movement

Whether you've been fighting for decades or this is your first act of resistance, you belong here. Bring your voice, your energy, and your commitment to good trouble. Together, we'll march not just through our neighborhoods, but toward a more perfect union.

*Comfortable walking shoes recommended. Water and snacks provided. All peaceful participants welcome.*

**Stand up. March on. Make good trouble.**

title: Support Immigrants at the Naturalization Ceremony, Strawberry Bank, Portsmouth.
description:
This 4th of July, Celebrate the True Builders of America — Immigrants.

This Independence Day, we invite you to stand in joyful, visible support of immigrants — the people who have long shaped the heart and future of New Hampshire and the United States.

From 9:30 to 11:30 AM, we’ll be gathering at Strawbery Banke Museum in Portsmouth, NH, in solidarity with those participating in a naturalization ceremony from 10:00 to 11:30 AM. Together, we’ll welcome new citizens and celebrate the enduring contributions of immigrant communities across the state and the nation.

From the mills of Manchester to the farms of the North Country, from Somali entrepreneurs in Concord to Guatemalan families in Nashua, immigrants have always been at the center of our shared story. Their work, culture, and courage have helped build this country. Their struggles and triumphs continue to strengthen it.

While others may try to replace patriotism with exclusion, we choose a different path. We choose community over cruelty, belonging over division, and joy over fear. Across New Hampshire, we will come together to uplift immigrant voices and show that freedom means justice for all — not just some.


Let’s reclaim the “big tent” for democracy — not a circus of fear, but a celebration of inclusion, dignity, and hope.

description:

title: Proud and Free: United for Trans Power
description:
Join us for #ProudandFree: United for Trans Power¨

The Supreme Court issued its ruling in U.S. v. Skrmetti, a challenge brought by three transgender adolescents, their families, and a Memphis-based medical provider against a Tennessee law banning gender-affirming hormone therapies for transgender people under 18.

The Supreme Court has failed to protect families’ freedoms and allowed politicians’ targeting of transgender youth’s healthcare needs to stand. This is a painful setback, but the Court left us with other tools to fight back against the political extremists targeting transgender people’s safety and dignity.

We are coming together in a "PROUD AND FREE: National Week of Action" to support trans people, push back on disinformation, and affirm that our communities are united for trans power.

🏛️ What is U.S. v. Skrmetti? A lawsuit filed by @ACLU, @LambdaLegal, @ACLU of Tennessee and Akin Gump on behalf of transgender youth and their families challenging Tennessee’s categorical ban (SB1) on gender-affirming medical care for transgender youth.

🏳️‍⚧️ Why does it matter? This case is about the constitutionality of states banning access to critical medical care for trans minors, particularly gender-affirming care. This could have nationwide impact on access to care, trans rights, and other sex-based discrimination by the government.

JOIN US in an action in your community for activations various days after the decision in support to the trans community!

📍 Event details coming soon! Please find events in your state or city.

🏛️ What is U.S. v. Skrmetti? A lawsuit filed by @ACLU, @LambdaLegal, @ACLU of Tennessee and Akin Gump on behalf of transgender youth and their families challenging Tennessee’s categorical ban (SB1) on gender-affirming medical care for transgender youth.

🏳️‍⚧️ Why does it matter? This case is about the constitutionality of states banning access to critical medical care for trans minors, particularly gender-affirming care. This could have nationwide impact on access to care, trans rights, and other sex-based discrimination by the government.

JOIN US in an action in your community for activations various days after the decision in support to the trans community!

title: Bethel Defends Democracy: Social Justice
description:
Please join us for our 17th consecutive rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday June 28th, 11am -12:30pm, our focus will be on Social Justice.

Social justice is the concept of creating a society where everyone has equal rights, opportunities, and treatment, regardless of their background or circumstances. It addresses systemic inequalities and aims to ensure fair and just outcomes for all individuals. Social justice is not just about treating everyone the same (equality), but also about recognizing that some individuals and groups may need additional support (equity) to overcome historical disadvantages and achieve similar outcomes.  

You are in for a treat because we will have the leaders of the Justice Southbury group as our speakers this week!  This group formed as a result of George Floyd's murder and has recently celebrated their 5 year anniversary of consecutive rallies every Sunday afternoon in Southbury.  We'll be welcoming back Jeremy Farrell who was our amazing speaker at our Spread Love, Not Hate rally, and looking forward to learning as well from the other fantastic leaders Rick Richardson and his inspiring daughter, Julia Richardson.

Barry Seroff will be back to fill our square with live music. He will also share a few words about his "Empathy is the Cure" project, which is a music series that raises money and good for local charities.  It takes place every 2nd Sunday at Molton Java.

The rally is non-partisan. What this means is that like-minded people from diverse backgrounds are participating and are vital to our rallies. Defending Democracy crosses party lines: we have registered Republicans, Unaffiliated, Democrats, and non-voters, all coming together to fight for the rights of “We the People” to determine the type of society we want to live in.

There will be something for everyone. We'll have speakers, we'll rally with our signs, we'll take a short march and we'll have live music. We also like to end each week with a sing-a-long.

Never miss information about upcoming rallies by scanning the QR code at our rally to register for our rally newsletter. You can also provide feedback on what you'd like to see at future rallies. 

A sign-making table will also be available, complete with all the necessary supplies, for young and old to make signs for the rally.

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

There are 2 small benches at the square and we will have a limited number of camping chairs. Please bring your own lawn or camping chair if you'd like.

Approximate Rally Schedule:

11:00 - 11:15  Assemble and rally at curb (You are welcome to arrive prior to 11:00 for extra curb time)

11:15 - 11:45 Speaker(s)

11:45 - Noon Rally at curb with chant leader

Noon - 12:20 March with chant leader

12:20   Closing Song

12:30   Disperse

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week. The food pantry greatly appreciates the donations each week!  Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but some special requests from the food pantry include:

sunscreen 

bug spray

Neither can be bought with SNAP but are vital for folks working outdoors in the summer or for kids who will be attending outdoor camps while school is out. Smaller containers that would fit inside a lunchbox are ideal size!

 We are currently lowest on baking supplies, pudding, and jello. Pudding and jello can either be the box mix or predone cups. 

Spices, Coffee and Baking supplies are always needed.

Individually packaged items. If you bought a variety pack of something like granola bars or instant oatmeal and discovered there's a flavor you won't eat, please give us the individual packs out of box.

Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

SMALL empty detergent bottles

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally. We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking. It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting, marching, themes with speakers, live music, fun trinkets, sign making. We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots. The lot that is very close to the rally location, PT Barnum Square, is behind the municipal center.

Although all street parking is public, we ask that you please not park in the limited parking spots in front of our local businesses, but definitely enjoy our beautiful towns restaurants and shops after the rally! 
Thank you 😊

title: Elbows Up For Canada
description:
Join us in a collaborative “Elbows Up for Canada” visibility event Saturday July 5, from 10am-12pm. at the Pittsburg, NH Border Crossing.
Sponsored by Coos NH Indivisible, North Country Resilience, Central NH Indivisible and friends.

Please be advised that the map is a little off due to this location not having an actual street address.  Use latitude and longitude: 45.253095, -71.205214 as a location in Pittsburg, NH. 

If you might plan to cross the border, don't forget your passport!

 
Carpooling is encouraged due to limited parking.  Carpool Options:
 
7:30 departure Marshall’s parking lot Tenney Mountain Highway, Plymouth
9:00 a.m. departure Municipal Lot behind Ducret's Sporting Goods, Colebrook

We will take photos at the iconic side-by-side monuments, one in Canada and the other is in the US, with approximately 18 inches of no man’s land in between.  Bring snacks, signs and flags.  
 
The Elbows Up movement is a coalition of American and Canadian advocacy groups committed to celebrating and strengthening the historic friendship between the United States and Canada and promoting grassroots support for continued US-Canada cooperation across economic, environmental, and security issues.
 
"In an era when division seems to dominate headlines, we want to show that the spirit of friendship and cooperation is alive and well along our shared border," co-organizer Audrey Bourriaud said. "These rallies prove that ordinary citizens on both sides want to build bridges, not walls."

Maps and directions:  https://www.ezbordercrossing.com/list-of-border-crossings/pittsburg-chartierville/

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON:
