title: Rally in Mentor to say NO to Cuts, Raids, and War--Congressman Joyce--HELP!!
description:
Come and join members of Ohio District 14 as we stand together to protest the harmful actions of the Trump Administration.     We gather every Friday from 10-11:30 along Mentor Avenue in Eleanor Garfield Park to say that we do not approve of Donald Trump's plan to cut funding for vital programs like Medicaid and Snap.  We do not approve of Donald Trump's plan to tear families apart by forcibly removing non-dangerous immigrants in our communities.   And we do not approve of Donald Trump (who called himself the "Peace President") bombing Iran without the approval of Congress and the people of the United States.   

We have reached out to Congressman Dave Joyce with our concerns about the harm of the Trump Administration, but we have not heard back with specific and reassuring responses.  And we have questions for the Congressman.  We want to know why Congressman Joyce voted to cut Medicaid and Snap.   We want to know why Congressman Joyce is allowing the Trump administration to terrify immigrants in our communities.  We want to know why Congressman Joyce did not take a stand against bombing Iran--an aggressive move that could be the start of the United States going to war in the Middle East.   All of these actions will cause harm to Congressman Joyce's constituents.  

***Congressman Joyce, we want you to stand up for the health, wellbeing, and safety of your constituents.  Please come and join us.  We need your help saying "NO" to the harmful behavior of the Trump administration. ***

Attendees:
Please bring friends and family and family-friendly signs.  Children have been joining us now that school is out.

Feel free to bring a chair, and join for any amount of time you are able.    Please park in the lower lot and walk up the hill to our protest site if you are able.   Leave the upper lot open for elders and families with young children.  Please do not park on the grass as vendors need to set up in this area for the Mentor Farmers Market.   

If you are able, please bring non-expired food and personal care items to donate to our local food pantries.   Food items include canned proteins, peanut butter and jelly, canned fruits and vegetable, and shelf stable food items such as grains, pasta, and cereal.  Personal care items include hand soap, toilet paper, tissues, paper towels, tampons, and diapers.


*A core principle behind all events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants not to engage with drivers, passers-by, and counter protestors who have different ideas than ours and show this in an unkind manner.  We will not return the hurt and anger.  We have an opportunity to show kindness and bridge the divide.  Let's take this opportunity.  Our nation needs this.*

This event is hosted by Ohio District 14 Partners--A coalition of pro-democracy groups in Ohio District 14.    June 27th marked our 20th event.

***Note--This event used to be held in front of the building that houses Congressman Joyce's office--8500 Station St., The Matchworks Building.   We used to enter the building in small groups to talk with the staff members in the Congressman's office while others protested on the sidewalk in front of the building.  Our group grew from 3 people to 60 people in 8 weeks.    We were not permitted to park in the lot in large numbers, so we decided to move to Eleanor Garfield Park.   

Individuals are permitted to park and enter the Matchworks Building to talk to staff members in the Congressman's Office on the third floor on M-F from 9-5.   We strongly encourage you to do this.  This action is a great way to protect and improve democracy.

title: Polk County Wants TRAINS — NOT INTERSTATES

location.venue: District One Florida Department of Transportation Headquarters

description:
# Polk County Wants TRAINS — NOT INTERSTATES
### Bartow, FL
#### W Van Fleet and N Broadway Ave
**8 am - 12 pm**
**Hosted by [Defund Oligarchy Blessed by Liberty](https://www.blessedbyliberty.org/)**

FDOT and the Polk County BOCC are planning an interstate extension that would cut through Lake Wales, Davenport, and other parts of eastern Polk County, in an effort to promote future development. 

But all proposed routes threaten critical areas: Bok Tower, family farms, or the habitat of the Blushing Scrub Balm—a rare native plant found nowhere else on Earth. Despite the rapid pace of new development, rents remain high and affordable housing is scarce. We are facing record-high foreclosure rates and thousands of vacant homes. 

So who is this development really for? Certainly not the people of Polk County. What will this mean for our already strained water supply? 

We must act now—protect Polk County! Protect the Blushing Scrub Balm. Polk County is not for sale. Let's stand up for public transit, and say NO WAY to the interstate. 

There is another option that FDOT refuses to consider: the NO-BUILD alternative. Join us for a sign-waving event on the public sidewalk as we deliver letters to our county officials. Let your voice be heard.

### Location & Instructions 
- Meet on the sidewalk at the intersection of Van Fleet & Broadway.
- FDOT office is 801 N Broadway Ave. 
- Don't forget to pick up a free slurpee across the street for free slurpee day.
- Bring signs & Florida state flags.
- Come early or come late. You don't have to stay the whole time. Come to wave a sign or come to learn more. We will have supplies for letter writing available. 
- This will be a reoccurring assembly to raise awareness in the months leading up to FDOT's meeting at the end of this year. Our goal is to inform commuters and get this issue on people's radar. As well as to deliver letters and provide further resources on how to follow-up with FDOT and County Commissioners.

title: Protest against sheriff ice contract
description:
**Protest Against the 287(g) Agreement at Lake County Sheriff’s Office**

Join us in standing up for our community! We are gathering to protest the recent decision by the Lake County Sheriff’s Office to implement the 287(g) agreement with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). This agreement empowers local law enforcement to act as immigration agents, increasing fear and distrust among our residents, particularly those from immigrant backgrounds.

The 287(g) program threatens public safety by discouraging individuals from reporting crimes or seeking help from law enforcement. It fosters an environment of fear, leading to division and suspicion within our community. We believe in a Lake County where everyone feels safe and supported, regardless of their immigration status.

Come together with us to voice our concerns and demand that our local leaders prioritize community safety and unity over divisive immigration policies. Your voice matters—let’s stand in solidarity for a more inclusive and compassionate


Together, we can make a difference!

title: 50 Days of Shame - Arkansas
description:
📣 STATEWIDE PROTEST: “50 DAYS OF SHAME” — Little Rock, Saturday 7/12

🛑 One state. One voice. One protest.
📍 LITTLE ROCK - Under the I-30 Overpass 
      (Next to the Courtyard Hotel in Downtown Little Rock)
⏰ 12:30PM - 3:00PM

🎯 We are demanding an end to fascist politics, to government corruption, and to the ongoing betrayal of the people of Arkansas. This is a protest against Arkansas lawmakers (congresspeople, senators, Governor Sanders, etc) and to shame them for their actions in Arkansas and pandering to the Trump Administration. The central theme of this protest is to demand that they DO THEIR JOBS and REPRESENT US!

☮️ The People’s Protests and Marches of AR and 50501 AR are dedicated to providing spaces for non-violent and peaceful demonstrations that provide community and hope to Arkansans. Violence and illegal behavior (vandalism, etc) will not be tolerated. 

On Saturday, July 12th, The People’s Protests and Marches of Arkansas and 50501 Arkansas are joining forces with organizers across the country for a nationwide day of resistance — one protest in every state. In Arkansas, Little Rock will be the only protest location, and we are calling on every region across the state to rise up and show up.

This day is part of the “50 Days of Shame” campaign — a direct call to our state representatives and senators to do their jobs: represent the people, not the Trump Administration. 

While they remain silent or complicit in the face of authoritarianism, we will not.
While they ignore economic injustice, environmental collapse, and attacks on our rights, we will rise.

🔥 Arkansas Issues to Protest on 7/12:

📚 Attacks on Education
	•	Book bans, censorship, DEI   
             rollbacks, school defunding, and the 
             LEARNS Act

🏥 Healthcare Failures
	•	Rural hospital closures, 
             Medicaid/Medicare cuts, anti-  
             trans laws, abortion bans, 
             maternal health crisis

🏛️ Government Corruption
	•	Power grabs, gerrymandering, 
             silencing public input

🏳️‍🌈 Anti-LGBTQ+ Laws
	•	Targeting trans youth, erasing 
             LGBTQ+ identities

💸 Poverty & Injustice
	•	Low wages, union-busting, cuts 
             to social safety nets like SNAP, racial 
             injustice 

🌲 Environmental Harm
	•	Pollution, clearcutting, lack of 
             clean water protections, natural 
             disaster relief, and assistance to 
             our farmers

🗳️ Attacks on Democracy
	•	Voter suppression, restricting 
             ballot initiatives, lack of due 
             process for immigrants, attacks 
             on D.E.I groups 

🚨 Police Overreach
	•	No accountability, over-policing, 
             rising militarization, militarization 
             of our police, ICE overreach 

🏚️ Housing Crisis
	•	Evictions, unaffordable rent, 
             weak renter protections

🎖️Neglect of Veterans
	•	 Underfunded VA support, lack of   
              healthcare, housing, and mental 
              health resources for those who  
              served


🎒 What to Bring:

✅ WATER - PLEASE COME HYDRATED!

✅ Lawn chairs - there won’t be any places to sit. If you need to be able to sit down, please bring a lawn chair!

✅ Protest Signs – Show the faces and names of Arkansas reps and senators. Call out their silence and complicity with bold slogans like “Do Your Job” or “Shame Has a Name.”

✅ Puppets/artistic satire – Get creative. Bring symbolic or satirical puppets and figurines of state leaders who’ve failed us.

✅ Protest Umbrellas – Reuse your decorated umbrellas from the 6/14 No Kings March, or bring a blank one to customize on-site.

✅ American Flags – Reclaim the flag for the people. 

✅ Creative Expression - bring art, costumes, and any other ways in which you would like to show creativity. 


The People’s Protests and Marches of AR and 50501 Arkansas are joining forces with other organizers and organizations from around the state to make this possible. We will also be working with these groups on coordinating buses, carpooling, and other travel accommodations from areas across Arkansas. Please stay tuned for a list of participating organizations and organizers as well as carpooling efforts.

Let’s remind them: We are watching. We are voting. We are not going away.
Join us in Little Rock and help make Arkansas impossible to ignore.


Sponsored by The People’s Protests and Marches and Indivisible LRCA. 

***The People’s Protests and Marches is a non-partisan group***

title: WIthout Due process Freedom is Just A Dream
description:
PEACEFUL sign holding rally  Please join us on Tuesday, July 1 and/or Tuesday, July 15, 2025 to show our outrage over the cruelty of ICE agents in their violation of people’s rights. We are showing up to defend our right to due process guaranteed to all people on US soil by the 5th and 14th amendments of our Constitution. Masked men (& women), without identifying themselves and without providing any judicial warrants, are disappearing people off the streets of our communities. People are being taken from their homes, from their jobs, from their cars, from their appointments with immigration, babies are being separated from their mothers, & undocumented foster children are being taken from their foster families. Some of these people have been sent to detention centers and/or to a prison in El Salvador and some are sent to unknown locations without any communication with their families, communities, and/or legal representation. This administration has stated they will look into deporting American Citizens. Who will be next? Will it be someone you love? Will it be you?  We are exercising our right to peacefully hold signs on public sidewalks on the Big Bend and Highway 141 overpass in Twin Oaks. Make signs, bring cowbells and big voices. Be sure to bring water to stay hydrated during these hot summer temps. Please leave no trace; do not litter. Note that nearby restroom facilities are limited.  If any individuals attempt to disrupt the rally by recording, shouting, or engaging with you, please remain composed. We suggest using cow bells or whistles or your favorite patriotic song to gently deter any disturbances; our focus must remain on our cause. Disruptors seeking confrontation will be ignored. Our chants will continue to amplify our message.  Parking is available at the Twin Oaks City Hall. The address is 1381 Big Bend Rd, Twin Oaks 63021. If you plan to stand on the north side of the overpass, there is a paved path leading down to the north side. There are no steps, but the path is sloped. It is a little less than a tenth of a mile walk from the TO City Hall parking lot to the overpass. If you plan to stand on the south side of the overpass, please cross Big Bend at the crosswalk at the entrance to Schnucks parking lot (next to Walgreens) or park on the south side of Big Bend. This lot is about 0.2 mile walk to overpass. There is not a safe place to cross Big Bend at the intersection of the overpass. Please use sidewalks and pedestrian crosswalks. This is a very high traffic area at rush hour.
Location
Twin Oaks Town Hall, 1381 Big Bend Rd, Ballwin, MO 63021, USA
Scheduled for
Tuesday, July 1, 2025 at 4:00 PM
Duration
2 hours

title: Power to the People
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

It's that time again! We need to remain steadfast in the fact that We the People have the Power. So this protest's theme will be Power to the People! Sick of all the chaos and dismantling of our country? Then this protest is for you, The People! You can  find us on Indivisible as South Suburban Relentless. Protect Our Rights. description:

Join us to support Independence without Tyranny.
This Fourth of July, we're reclaiming America's promise: Freedom for all! Justice for all! NO KINGS!

title: March for Integrity (Nevada)
description:
The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: Forests for Indy - March from IFA to the City-County Council Meeting on Monday July 7th
description: Summer is here and we are more grateful than ever for our urban forests and the relief they provide us. It is also budget season, and our forests need our help to continue helping us! Unfortunately, Indianapolis continues to lose urban forests and canopy and all the benefits they provide - heat mitigation, carbon capture, storm water management, beautification and quality of life. There is only one way that this destruction ends - with forest friends demanding change. Please join our "Forests for Indy" volunteers and march to the Council meeting to do exactly that. The Councilors see and notice us and our advocacy makes a difference. We are pushing for: the creation of a "forest fund" (Marion County Urban Forest Preservation Fund), for an agency to manage this fund and properly steward the remaining forest in Marion County, and for the allocation of money in the 2026 budget for the acquisition of urban forest.

title: PCH Freedom Rally Sunset Beach (Huntington Beach)
description:
While Trump and his allies cling to power with bluster and spectacle, we're coming together—calmly, clearly, and courageously—to remind the nation where real power lives: in the people.

From Seal Beach to Dana Point, neighbors will line Pacific Coast Highway in a coordinated demonstration of love, unity, and resistance. We’ll raise our flags, lift our voices, and take up space—not to divide, but to defend what’s worth fighting for: democracy, dignity, and each other.
This isn’t just a rally. It’s a moment of good trouble—the kind Congressman John Lewis taught us to make when injustice rises and silence is not an option.

This is a stand for:
Reproductive freedom
LGBTQ+ rights
Climate justicw
Voting rights
Immigrant dignity
And the right to speak freely, live safely, and dream boldly!


Our message is simple: America doesn’t belong to a king. It belongs to all of us. And patriotism isn’t about parades or personality cults—it’s about showing up for one another and protecting what we love.

Join us on Saturday, July 19th, from 12–2 PM, at any of our coastal rally points. From Seal Beach to Dana Point, we’ll be standing together. Wear red, white, or blue if you’d like, bring signs, water, and sunscreen—and most importantly, bring your belief that a better future is still possible.
This is a peaceful, family-friendly action. Hand-held signs only. No yelling at counter-protesters—we de-escalate, we don’t engage. This is about showing up with joy, conviction, and a whole lot of courage.

Let’s make good trouble together—because our future depends on it.

location.venue: Pacific Coast Highway at the Huntington Beach Pier

description:
While Trump and his allies cling to power with bluster and spectacle, we're coming together—calmly, clearly, and courageously—to remind the nation where real power lives: in the people.

From Seal Beach to Dana Point, neighbors will line Pacific Coast Highway in a coordinated demonstration of love, unity, and resistance. We’ll raise our flags, lift our voices, and take up space—not to divide, but to defend what’s worth fighting for: democracy, dignity, and each other.

This isn’t just a rally. It’s a moment of good trouble—the kind Congressman John Lewis taught us to make when injustice rises and silence is not an option.

This is a stand for:
Reproductive freedom
LGBTQ+ rights
Climate justice
Voting rights
Immigrant dignity
And the right to speak freely, live safely, and dream boldly!

Our message is simple: America doesn’t belong to a king. It belongs to all of us. And patriotism isn’t about parades or personality cults—it’s about showing up for one another and protecting what we love.
Join us on Saturday, July 19th, from 12–2 PM, at any of our coastal rally points.

From Seal Beach to Dana Point, we’ll be standing together. Wear red, white, or blue if you’d like, bring signs, water, and sunscreen—and most importantly, bring your belief that a better future is still possible.

This is a peaceful, family-friendly action. Hand-held signs only. No yelling at counter-protesters—we de-escalate, we don’t engage. This is about showing up with joy, conviction, and a whole lot of courage.

Let’s make good trouble together—because our future depends on it.
Full details: https://indivisibleca47.org

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Stop the Cuts to VA Care – Rally for Veterans and Workers!
description:
The Save Our VA (SVOA) Coalition is asking you to stand together to say NO to cuts in veterans' care and YES to solidarity with VA workers and VA healthcare. Join us outside the main entrance of the Tucson VA (6th Ave) on Monday, July 1st, from 7:00 to 8:30 a.m. as we rally to oppose the appointment of a new Southern VA Director poised to deepen the harmful cuts initiated under Representative Ciscomani and the Trump administration. SOVA includes Veterans for Peace, Common Defense, Southern AZ Community Activists, Working Families Power and Honest Arizona. 

📍 Location: Tucson VA Medical Center, Main Entrance on 6th Avenue
🗓️ Date: Monday, July 1, 2025
🕖 Time: 7:00 a.m. – 8:30 a.m.
✊ Type of Event: Rally, Protest & Press Conference

Doctors are resigning. Staff are walking out. Veterans are watching. These dangerous staffing shortages and cuts are dismantling the care our veterans earned through their service. This is not acceptable.

Why We’re Showing Up

💥 To Oppose Further Cuts to the VA healthcare system in Tucson that harm both patients and providers.

👩‍⚕️👨‍⚕️ To Stand in Solidarity with VA Staff who are overworked, under-supported, and deserve our full backing.

🪖 To Support Veterans who are demanding accountability and transparency as their care is put at risk.

🙏 To Say Thank You to the healthcare professionals still showing up every day for our veterans despite ongoing threats to their working conditions.

Bring Your Voice. Bring Your Sign. Bring Your Solidarity.
We invite veterans, workers, union members, patients, and allies to stand together and raise our voices. This is our VA. This is our community. Let's make sure leadership hears us loud and clear.

📢 Signs, chants, bull horns, music and community power encouraged.
💡 Water and shade will be available.
🚌 Public transit accessible; parking nearby.

RSVP Today to Stand Up for Veterans and the Workers
Together, we’ll show Trump and Representative Ciscomani -- that we won’t stand by while care for our veterans is sacrificed.

title: March for Integrity (Oregon)
description:
The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in Salem, Oregon, to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

title: Comunidades Unidas Jamás Serán Vencidas
description:
Join us this 4th of July as we reclaim what independence truly means. While many celebrate freedom, millions of immigrants in this country are still living in fear, under attack by unjust laws and racist systems.

We’re gathering in solidarity with all immigrant communities, to demand dignity, protection, and real freedom for all. Because as the Pledge of Allegiance says: “with liberty and justice for all” — and we’re here to remind this country to live up to those words.


✊🏽 This is a PEACEFUL protest. No
reckless behavior will be tolerated. We stand united in resistance, but we do so with discipline and purpose.

📢 What to Bring:
     ✅️ Posters, banners, and flags to amplify our message.
     ✅️ Your voice, your passion, and your commitment to justice.

⚠️ Important Guidelines:
     🚶Stay on sidewalks = DO NOT block streets or intersections. Our presence is powerful--let's keep it peaceful and organized.
     🚔 Respect law enforcement and fellow protesters.
     🗣  Make your voice heard without violence or disruption.

♻️ Keep Our Community Clean:
Pick up after yourself — NO LITTERING! If you see trash, please pick it up. Let's respect our space.

**********
Acompáñanos este 4 de Julio mientras recuperamos el verdadero significado de la independencia. Mientras muchos celebran la libertad, millones de inmigrantes siguen viviendo con miedo, siendo atacados por leyes injustas y sistemas racistas.

Nos reunimos en solidaridad con todas las comunidades inmigrantes, para exigir dignidad, protección y libertad real para todos. Como dice el Juramento a la Bandera: “con libertad y justicia para todos” — y estamos aquí para recordarle a este país que cumpla con esas palabras.


✊🏽 Esta es una protesta PACÍFICA. No se tolerará ningún comportamiento imprudente. Nos mantenemos unidos en resistencia, pero lo hacemos con disciplina y propósito.

📢 Qué traer:
     ✅ Letreros, pósteres y banderas para amplificar nuestro mensaje.
     ✅ Tu voz, tu pasión y tu compromiso con la justicia.
⚠️ Reglas importantes:
     🚶 Mantente en las aceras—NO bloquees calles ni intersecciones. Nuestra presencia es poderosa—mantengámosla pacífica y organizada.
     🚔 Respeta a las fuerzas del orden y a tus compañeros manifestantes.
      🗣️ Haz que tu voz se escuche sin violencia ni interrupciones.
♻️ Mantengamos limpia nuestra comunidad: Recoge tu basura—¡NO ENSUCIES! Si ves basura, recógela. Respetemos nuestro espacio.

title: Independence Day March Against Fear
description:
🎉 JOIN US FOR A JULY 4TH MARCH WITH MEANING! 🎉  
March Against Fear: Stronger Together  
📅 Friday, July 4  
⏰ 9:00 AM  
📍 St. Andrew’s Lutheran Church, 629 8th St NE, Hickory, NC 28601   

Start your Independence Day standing up for ALL of us! Join Indivisible Citizens of Catawba Valley, local educators, healthcare workers, LGBTQ+ neighbors, Latinos, artists, and residents from every corner of our community as we march together in celebration of hope, courage, and unity.

🖐️ Bring a sign that shows the world who YOU are and what YOU believe in. A few ideas:    
“I am a gay man entitled to equal rights and justice”   
“I am a profiled woman of color”

title: Virginia Beach Free America Protest March
description:
CELEBRATE FREEDOM. IGNITE YOUR REBELLION!

Join us at the "Virginia Beach Free America Protest March" from 5 to 8 pm on July 4th on the Virginia Beach Boardwalk. This event is organized by Virginia Beach Mavericks, a local Indivisible organization, and this Fourth of July march is also part of the nationwide Women's March Free America Weekend. The plan is for protestors to carry their signs and march along the boardwalk between 16th and 33rd streets. Begin at the closest location to your parking, and move along the boardwalk south or north, turning around and heading in the opposite direction at 16th and 33rd. Yes, it will be crowded. Yes, parking will be hard. And no, we do not have a permit, and we will not have protest marshals or safety personnel. 

But it is essential to make our voices heard, especially on Independence Day. We must FREE AMERICA from the grip of greedy billionaires who rig the system for themselves, from arbitrary firings and a flood of unlawful orders, from poverty and the rigged system where the wealthy live large while the middle class foots the bill, and from the grip of hate and the politics of fear!

Independence Day is about the fight for freedom. The American Revolution was a stand against tyranny and kings. That same spirit has lived on—from the Boston Tea Party to the Underground Railroad, from Stonewall to the Civil Rights Movement.

America is in crisis. Real democracy feels out of reach. Freedom is in trouble.

This July 4th weekend, while the U.S. marks Independence Day, we’ll gather across the country—on porches, in town squares, backyards, and streets—to stand for real freedom and build a vision of a Free America brick by brick. 

Free America is wherever we are. Free America is whatever we make it.

THIS IS YOUR INVITATION TO TAKE IT BACK. Our freedom. Our people. Our rebellion.

They want us scared, divided, and alone. They don’t want us to dream about freedom. But that’s exactly what we have to do.

This Fourth of July, we will be on the boardwalk with songs of freedom and joy. The dream of American freedom belongs to all of us, and we will not stop in our pursuit of its promise, now or ever. This is also a local Indivisible event!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Marshfield Diversity Rally

location.venue: Marshfield Town Green(next to town hall)

description:
Marshfield is always striving to be a more diverse community and welcoming to strangers. One way the town has done this is to issue proclamations recognizing communities in the town on specific days and months. Unfortunately, for the first time in three years, there was no proclamation issued to recognize Pride Month.

The reason there is no proclamation is that the chair of the select board had the Pride Proclamation line item removed from the agenda in an early June meeting. Thanks to the efforts of community members, advocates, and allies, the Pride Proclamation line item has been added to the agenda for Monday's Selectboard meeting. At the meeting, the Pride Proclamation will be voted on by the full selectboard on the last day of Pride Month. Unfortunately, there is no guarantee Proclamation will pass.

This is why on Monday, June 30th, we are having a rally at the town green to show the select board that Marshfield is a community that supports diversity and inclusion. Starting at 5:00, we'll meet at the town green on the corner of Moraine St. and Snow Rd. in Marshfield center. This is a family-friendly event, so please bring your G-rated signs expressing support for the LGBTQ+ community and the passing of the Pride Proclamation.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*
accessibility_notes: In addition, if you are a Marshfield resident, we are asking people to testify in support of the bill at the select board meeting. You can do this in person at town hall by signing in and requesting to speak before the select board meeting starts. If you cannot attend in person, a virtual option is available to you. Anyone attending virtually via the town-provided Zoom link, the team is asking them to change their profile picture to the Harvey Milk profile. Click the link to get the image. https://www.mdtc.blog/getinvolved

title: Freedom Friday - Money for People.  Not for War.

address_lines: North Hamilton Street & East Trent Avenue

description:
This a local Indivisible event!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

In the words of Tupac Shakur "They got money for the war, but can't feed the poor."  

WE ARE ALSO COLLECTING FOOD PANTRY SUPPLIES FOR OUR FRIENDS AT SPECTRUM Center Spokane.  Let's make Tupac proud and show our community some love.  

They can really use peanut butter and tuna.  Spices are especially needed (salt, pepper, herbs, etc.)  4-Packs of TP, tampons.  Body wash, deodorant, etc in travel sizes.

Find me or Kim after the event and we will load up our cars.  

"As Israel's massive, unprovoked bombardment of Iran continues, Trump is weighing whether or not the United States should directly enter the war. This is the critical moment when we need to make it loud and clear that the people of this country reject another endless war. The National Iranian American Council, ANSWER Coalition, Palestinian Youth Movement, The People's Forum, and many other organizations are joining together to organize these actions.

A U.S. bombing campaign could easily spiral into "boots on the ground", massive casualties, and a regional or even global war with catastrophic consequences. And more and more of our tax dollars will be eaten up by the war machine rather than being used to meet human needs.
Just like George W. Bush was lying about "weapons of mass destruction" in Iraq, Trump and Netanyahu are lying about an Iranian nuclear weapons program. This is a war for regime change and a war to steal Iran's vast oil and gas resources. The people say NO!" (From the Answer Coalition)

Meet up afterwards (optional of course) at Northern Lights Brewing Co & Pub1003 E Trent Ave, Spokane, WA  99202

Peaceful sidewalk protest. Bring signs.   American flags are always wonderful too.

All across southern California, masked ICE agents are abducting people -- often without judicial warrants -- and sending them to filthy and abusive detention centers. Those of us who are unafraid to speak out and say this is wrong need to be the speak out for those who feel they need to hide.

title: Good Trouble
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Coined by civil rights leader Congressman John Lewis, "Good Trouble" is the action of coming together to take peaceful, non-violent action to challenge injustice and create meaningful change.

The civil rights leaders of the past have shown us the power of collective action. July 17th represents five years since the passing of Congressman John Lewis; on this day and on the following weekend,  communities across the country will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all. Our community has chosen to demonstrate  for these principles on SATURDAY JULY 19TH.

We are facing the most brazen rollback of civil rights in generations. The same forces that used violence against John Lewis and civil rights leaders for marching for justice on the Edmund Pettus Bridge are back, with billionaire backers, extremist leaders and authoritarian ambition. Our freedom to vote is being attacked with the attempt to pass laws that would block millions of Americans  from the polls.Trump and his allies are weaponizing racist voter suppression tactics to silence the voices of those who demand accountability, specifically targeting Black, Brown, immigrant and indigenous communities. 

We will gather on this day for a non-violent protest.  





*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

On July 17, the anniversary of Congressman John Lewis’s passing, we’re taking action across the country to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of Good Trouble.

We are currently facing the most brazen rollback of civil rights in generations. Whether you’re outraged by attacks on voting rights, the gutting of essential services, disappearances of our neighbors, or the assault on free speech and our right to protest – this movement is for you! “Get in good trouble, necessary trouble, and help redeem the soul of America.”  - Congressman John Lewis

Join us at the Rock Springs Chamber of Commerce on July 17th from 4:30PM – 6:30PM and bring your signs!! Food trucks will be on site! Bring chairs if you need them!

title: March for Freedom in the Springfield Midtown 4th of July Parade
description:
Come join us in the parade on the 4th of July! We will be participating alongside Greater Springfield Indivisible! 

The theme is freedom and patriotism for all! See you there!

From Midtown Neighborhood Associations Event post:

Springfield's Old-Fashioned 4th of July Parade & Celebration in Washington Park!
2025 Theme: "Good Neighbors, Strong Communities"
Date: Friday, July 4th, 2025
Time: 10:00am - 1:00pm-rain or shine-9:00am parade lineup on Drury Lane & Central

The 34th annual event takes place in Midtown, Springfield's largest nationally registered historic district and is open to all Springfield citizens for viewing along parade route parkways and ends with a celebration in historic Washington Park established in 1869. Parade entries include: Antique cars & trucks, scout troops or other non-profit groups, Victorian Ladies Drill Team, floats, decorated trucks, cars, bikes & scooters, etc.
This year's Grand Marshal is: Dr. Grenita Lathan, Superintendent of Springfield Public Schools.
The celebration at historic Washington Park follows the parade, between 11:00am and 1:00pm. The park celebration starts with Alberta Smith and her daughter Aubrey singing the National Anthem. There will be music, free water and ice cream from the Springfield Police "Cold Patrol" plus, free children's games! DNA BBQ food truck will offer a "special" for purchase at the event as well as their BBQ favorites.
Bring lawn chairs, and/or blankets to sit on. Prizes will be awarded for the following categories: Best Overall, Best Theme Interpretation ("Good Neighbors, Strong Communities"), Best Children's Float, Best Children's Marching Unit, Best Adult Float, and Best Adult Marching Unit

The parade begins at 10:00am at the intersection of Central and Drury Lane; heads west on Central to Benton Avenue; turns right/north on Benton, turns right/east on Calhoun by historic Drury President's home; turns left/north on Washington Avenue & passes through renovated historic Victorian homes; crosses Division Street; and finally turns right/east on Locust to end at Historic Washington Park where the celebration continues.

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON:
description:
Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of nonviolent action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

On July 17, the anniversary of Congressman John Lewis’s passing, we’re taking action across the country to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of Good Trouble.

From voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act to the criminalization of protest, the Trump administration is launching a full-scale attack on our civil and human rights. But we know the truth: in America, the power lies with the people, and we’re rising to prove it.

This is more than a protest; it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** A core principle behind our Good Trouble Lives On actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

title: Poughkeepsie, NY: Tell Rep Lawler to Stop Trump's Big Cruel Bill!
description:
Rep. Lawler is coming to Poughkeepsie to speak at a fundraiser with the Dutchess County GOP this Tuesday! Lawler in the past has voted to cut SNAP and Medicaid against the interests of his constituents--but he still has a chance to stop the budget cuts!

**Join us for a rally outside Lawler's fundraiser to tell him to vote NO on Trump's big cruel bill!**

Trump’s budget bill is quickly moving through Congress. The Senate is expected to pass the bill any day now, and then it will go onto the House for another vote. This bill would strip healthcare and food assistance from millions of Americans in order to pay for tax cuts for the wealthy. 

This bill is unacceptable, and Rep Lawler needs to know his constituents are angry for his past support of this bill and we demand he vote NO. 

*We'll meet on the sidewalk outside the Grandview where the fundraiser is taking place. RSVP for specific meetup and parking details.*

title: Peace, Protest, and Patriotism Hootenanny
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Independence Day is about the fight for freedom. The American Revolution was a stand against tyranny and kings. That same spirit has lived on—from the Boston Tea Party to the Underground Railroad, from Stonewall to the Civil Rights Movement.

America is in crisis. Real democracy feels out of reach. Freedom is in trouble. Warmongers are back at it, even as they cut funding for the rest of us.

This July 4th weekend, while the U.S. marks Independence Day, we’ll gather across the country—on porches, in town squares, backyards, and streets—to stand for real freedom and build a vision of a Free America brick by brick.

In Lancaster, Pennsylvania, we'll occupy space joyfully with music and song. Meet downtown Saturday July 5th at Penn Square from 10:30am-12:30pm to play and sing songs of PEACE, PROTEST, and PATRIOTISM. Revive Free America in our hearts, our city, our county and our country.

Free America is wherever we are. Free America is whatever we make it. This Saturday, July 5th, celebrate with music and singing.

They want us scared, divided, and alone. They don’t want us to dream about freedom. But that’s exactly what we have to do.

This Fourth of July weekend, on Saturday, July 5th, we will be in community downtown with songs of freedom and joy. The dream of American freedom belongs to all of us, and we will not stop in our pursuit of its promise, now or ever. 

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Hell No to the BBB Rally!
description:
Join Us to Let Congressman Rob Bresnahan Know That His Vote for the BBB is Shameful and Unacceptable!

In the coming days, the Republican controlled Senate will be considering the House Passed GOP Mega Bill from hell. The GOP’s reconciliation bill from the darkest corners of its ambitions passed the House of Representatives in DC in May and now the bill is before the Senate for consideration. This bill would negatively impact Medicaid, SNAP, and other programs and services in the state that millions of Pennsylvanians rely on!

Part of the GOP’s scheme with SNAP, Medicaid, and other programs is for a cost sharing requirement with the states. Pennsylvania would find it difficult if not impossible to pick up that fiscal slack, which would undermine these programs–just as the GOP cruelly intends. Not only that, the legislation intends to bury millions of people in red tape so that they can't get the life saving services they rely on!

Join For Our Future PA, Action Together NEPA, the Pennsylvania Policy Center, Pennsylvanians Together, storytellers from the community, and Senator Chris Coons at 11am on July 1st to hear about why Congressman Rob Bresnahan’s vote for the big, bloated, and ugly bill cannot be tolerated! title: "Good Trouble Lives On" honoring the legacy of John Lewis.  Hosted by Indivisible Lowell.
description:
What is “Good Trouble Lives On”?
Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people.

Coined by civil rights leader Congressman John Lewis, “Good Trouble” is the act of coming together to take peaceful, non-violent action to challenge injustice and create meaningful change. Good Trouble is marches, protests, service work – any action where communities come together, take a stand against wrongdoings, and speak truth to power.

The civil rights leaders of the past have shown us the power of collective action. That’s why on July 17, five years since the passing of Congressman John Lewis, we’re calling on Americans across the country to Make Good Trouble Together.

title: Copy of: Mondays @ McCormick's
description:
This is an EMERGENCY! Senate Protest Event in Philadelphia Continues This Week and For the Foreseeable Future.

Now called "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - Here's why:

We are living in a MAGA-republican Coup. We were warned. Now it's here!

Here at home our democratic rights are being eroded and the Trump/Musk team is putting us all in danger. The limits of Executive power against the courts are being tested every day. If Trump decides to ignore the courts, there is very little they can do to enforce their decisions and unless Congress acts, it would be a true constitutional crisis. (And so far, Congress is controlled by the MAGA movement and the Democrats have not done enough to stand up and fight back.) It could even spiral down into outright civil war as competing factions and states careen between untested solutions to protect their own interests and those of their constituents and funders. There is real harm being done across the entire domestic sector. Layoffs, program cuts for the needy and for the average US resident, persecution of law abiding immigrants and students and other activists for simply speaking their mind and organizing constitutionally protected protest. Fear is also their weapon.

Our international role is being flipped on its head - yes, the US has always had a questionable foreign policy, providing aid and promoting democracy and human rights - to a degree - on the one hand, while at the same time invading other countries for the good of corporate profits and geopolitical dominance. Trump considers a policy to outright invade counties like Mexico and Greenland in violation of international law and to extend US power - A clear expression of Empire! Trump is considering power grabs not unlike those that the Nazi regime in Germany perpetrated in search of "Lebensraum", (Living Space) a euphemism for territorial conquest. And they got away with it (for a while) because the people who stood up were either jailed, exiled or murdered. The rest were either regime supporters (Like the solid 30% base of the MAGA movement) or went along out of fear of retribution. We cannot let fear prevent us from standing up this time. History will judge us.

We now have a true oligarchy in the US and we must fight back!

The Trump administration’s illegal actions and relentless efforts to dismantle protections for vulnerable communities — both here in the U.S. and abroad— have made clear we are in the midst of an authoritarian takeover not unlike what has happened in Orban’s Hungary. 

His plan to "Own Gaza" and move out Palestinians is NOT a plan to destroy Hamas and increase Israeli security - it is ETHNIC CLEANSING pure and simple. It's a land grab. All for development rights and to secure a seaport access to natural gas deposits off the shore of Gaza in the Mediterranean Sea. The Levant gas field includes the shores of historic Palestine (Israel and Gaza), Syria, Lebanon and, on the opposite side, the island of Cyprus. This field is estimated to contain about 122 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. So it will accelerate the climate emergency. 

As we all know Trump/Musk plan to get rid of a number of government agencies that protect our health, livelihood and constitutional rights. - the EPA is on the hit list. The Department of Education is too. So, is the CDC, the NIH and many other important agencies that protect the US public.

As we all know - thousands have already been fired, causing chaos and havoc and real harm to both dedicated civil servants AND people served by life affirming programs voted on by the U.S. people and enacted, in most cases, by the U.S. Congress. The Administration may have authority to make staffing decisions, but as is the case with the Department of Education - many of these agencies can only be eliminated by acts of Congress - Trump has overstepped his legal authority.

Thankfully, the courts have, so far, acted as a check on much of Trumps clear and blatant abuses of executive power. But we cannot count on the courts, particularly the US Supreme court, which has been stacked by Trump appointees and ideologues friendly to executive power. 

Resistance is NOT futile - it is essential. 

We are launching "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - we will assemble peaceably - as is our constitutional right - outside Senator McCormick's Philadelphia office until Senator McCormick agrees to meet with us and support our demands: (These will change as conditions develop)

 1 - Stop voting for legislation inspired by Trump's project 2025 agenda - a plan to slash Medicaid, gut school lunch programs, and shut down nursing homes while handing more power to billionaires like Elon Musk. 

2- Roll back Trump's mean spirited and Unconstitutional funding pauses. Shutting down USAID is already killing people in need all over the World. Cuts to programs here in the US could do the same. Funding for these programs are up to the Congress and the US people to decide, not Trump! 

That's just for starters. Overall we want Senator McCormick to represent us all, not just his rich friends. We want Senator McCormick to DO HIS JOB!
The stakes could not be higher. The administration is pushing an authoritarian agenda that threatens our democracy, our rights, and the well-being of millions here at home and around the planet. 

We have the power to resist—and we must use every tool at our disposal to stop them.

title: Chuck the Clock — It’s Time for a Record-Breaking Vote-a-Rama!
description:
The Senate vote on the MAGA Murder Budget is imminent—and it’s time for Chuck to lead a Vote-a-Rama for the history books.

A vote-a-rama is a marathon Senate session where senators vote on a rapid-fire series of amendments—often dozens or even hundreds—usually tied to budget bills. It can go all night. There’s no cap on the number of amendments, which makes it a powerful tool to delay bad legislation, force tough votes, and shine a spotlight on what’s at stake. It’s procedural chaos—by design.

The longest vote-a-rama on record happened on March 13, 2008, with 44 roll-call votes over more than 10 hours. That’s the bar. Chuck can beat it.

The devastation buried in the BBB (Big Bad Bill) will harm millions of Americans. Every hour Democrats can delay this vote is an hour more for the public to learn what’s inside—and demand their Senators and Congressmembers stop it.

Join us, NY Communities for Change, and Food and Water Watch Saturday morning outside Chuck’s building to stiffen his spine, fuel his resolve, and make it clear:

He must use every tool—including a record-breaking vote-a-rama—to grind this bill to a halt.

title: Good Trouble Lives On in Dripping Springs!
description:
John Lewis, Congressman and Civil Rights Leader, championed engaging in GOOD TROUBLE, and in honor of him, we plan to have a PARADE around Dripping Springs.  We will be flying our American flags, tarting up our cars, trucks and motorcycles and showing our opposition to Trump and Company's UNconstitutional abuses and excesses.  

Our rights, and the future of our democracy are at stake, and we will not   remain silent.  Stand up and make your voices heard! Make Good Trouble!

We plan to have some fun while we exercise our First Amendment Right to Free Speech and Freedom of Assembly.

We shall meet on  Saturday, July 19th, 10 am at the  City Hall parking lot in Dripping Springs, at 511 Mercer Street.  

Instead of our traditional street corner protest at RR 12 and Hwy 290, we thought y'all would enjoy taking a little ride around the neighborhood, ending up for lunch at El Rey.

Bring signs, flags, shoe polish, bunting, pretty much anything you think might look great on (and not fall off) your vehicle.  Be fancy, dress up if you want, and Let's Ride for Democracy!

We will meet this time, not at Veterans Park (the DS Farmer's Market is there that Saturday), but right down Mercer Street at the DS City Hall parking lot.  It might be good to do any elaborate decorating before you show up, but we will also be working on our cars while we gather.

This is our way of letting our friends and neighbors know what we stand for, and what we will not fall for. 

Like always, our event will be peaceful, law-abiding, non-confrontational and non-violent.  We encourage everyone to de-escalate any unpleasant interactions with the public.  Smile and wave, even at those giving you the finger, or honking aggressively. 

We also ask that you leave all weapons at home, and do not intentionally offend the public by displaying profanity or vulgar words on signs or flags.

In light of recent events, our movement has evolved to include Anti-War sentiment, and slogans.  Peace and Justice at home, and abroad, is our goal.  

The nationwide "Good Trouble Lives On" events are mostly going to be held on Thursday, July 17th, the anniversary of John Lewis's passing, but upon reflection, we thought our crowd might prefer continuing our Saturday morning tradition.  So, we are meeting on Saturday, not Thursday, as that just seemed more our style.

Remember: We meet EVERY Saturday morning, at 10 am, usually at Veterans Park, and then walk on over to the intersection with our signs and flags, our smiles and waves. 

Call 512-829-1626 if you have any question as to whether bad weather or other contingencies may require us to move or cancel our protest.

description: We must come together and resist the oppressive Trump regime with unwavering strength. How can we celebrate this Fourth of July while our fellow citizens face relentless attacks? title: Mondays @ McCormick's
description:
This is an EMERGENCY! Senate Protest Event in Philadelphia Continues This Week and For the Foreseeable Future.

Now called "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - Here's why:

We are living in a MAGA-republican Coup. We were warned. Now it's here!

Here at home our democratic rights are being eroded and the Trump/Musk team is putting us all in danger. The limits of Executive power against the courts are being tested every day. If Trump decides to ignore the courts, there is very little they can do to enforce their decisions and unless Congress acts, it would be a true constitutional crisis. (And so far, Congress is controlled by the MAGA movement and the Democrats have not done enough to stand up and fight back.) It could even spiral down into outright civil war as competing factions and states careen between untested solutions to protect their own interests and those of their constituents and funders. There is real harm being done across the entire domestic sector. Layoffs, program cuts for the needy and for the average US resident, persecution of law abiding immigrants and students and other activists for simply speaking their mind and organizing constitutionally protected protest. Fear is also their weapon.

Our international role is being flipped on its head - yes, the US has always had a questionable foreign policy, providing aid and promoting democracy and human rights - to a degree - on the one hand, while at the same time invading other countries for the good of corporate profits and geopolitical dominance. Trump considers a policy to outright invade counties like Mexico and Greenland in violation of international law and to extend US power - A clear expression of Empire! Trump is considering power grabs not unlike those that the Nazi regime in Germany perpetrated in search of "Lebensraum", (Living Space) a euphemism for territorial conquest. And they got away with it (for a while) because the people who stood up were either jailed, exiled or murdered. The rest were either regime supporters (Like the solid 30% base of the MAGA movement) or went along out of fear of retribution. We cannot let fear prevent us from standing up this time. History will judge us.

We now have a true oligarchy in the US and we must fight back!

The Trump administration’s illegal actions and relentless efforts to dismantle protections for vulnerable communities — both here in the U.S. and abroad— have made clear we are in the midst of an authoritarian takeover not unlike what has happened in Orban’s Hungary. 

His plan to "Own Gaza" and move out Palestinians is NOT a plan to destroy Hamas and increase Israeli security - it is ETHNIC CLEANSING pure and simple. It's a land grab. All for development rights and to secure a seaport access to natural gas deposits off the shore of Gaza in the Mediterranean Sea. The Levant gas field includes the shores of historic Palestine (Israel and Gaza), Syria, Lebanon and, on the opposite side, the island of Cyprus. This field is estimated to contain about 122 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. So it will accelerate the climate emergency. 

As we all know Trump/Musk plan to get rid of a number of government agencies that protect our health, livelihood and constitutional rights. - the EPA is on the hit list. The Department of Education is too. So, is the CDC, the NIH and many other important agencies that protect the US public.

As we all know - thousands have already been fired, causing chaos and havoc and real harm to both dedicated civil servants AND people served by life affirming programs voted on by the U.S. people and enacted, in most cases, by the U.S. Congress. The Administration may have authority to make staffing decisions, but as is the case with the Department of Education - many of these agencies can only be eliminated by acts of Congress - Trump has overstepped his legal authority.

Thankfully, the courts have, so far, acted as a check on much of Trumps clear and blatant abuses of executive power. But we cannot count on the courts, particularly the US Supreme court, which has been stacked by Trump appointees and ideologues friendly to executive power. 

Resistance is NOT futile - it is essential. 

We are launching "Monday's at McCormick's" each Monday at noon - rain or shine - we will assemble peaceably - as is our constitutional right - outside Senator McCormick's Philadelphia office until Senator McCormick agrees to meet with us and support our demands: (These will change as conditions develop)

 1 - Stop voting for legislation inspired by Trump's project 2025 agenda - a plan to slash Medicaid, gut school lunch programs, and shut down nursing homes while handing more power to billionaires like Elon Musk. 

2- Roll back Trump's mean spirited and Unconstitutional funding pauses. Shutting down USAID is already killing people in need all over the World. Cuts to programs here in the US could do the same. Funding for these programs are up to the Congress and the US people to decide, not Trump! 

That's just for starters. Overall we want Senator McCormick to represent us all, not just his rich friends. We want Senator McCormick to DO HIS JOB!
The stakes could not be higher. The administration is pushing an authoritarian agenda that threatens our democracy, our rights, and the well-being of millions here at home and around the planet. 

We have the power to resist—and we must use every tool at our disposal to stop them.

title: People over Profit: Billionaires Shouldn’t Rule America
description:
## **People over Profit: Billionaires Shouldn’t Rule America**

The United States is not a corporation, and our government is not a for-profit enterprise. Elon Musk is not a government official. He’s a billionaire with no accountability to the American people, and nobody voted for him. Our democracy deserves better.

Musk and Trump will only be defeated by a massive, bipartisan movement of everyday Americans standing up against corruption, authoritarianism, and huge tax breaks for the rich, while fighting for the programs that working people need.

** This is a BIPARTISAN, PEACEFUL Protest** 
**No violence or Destruction of Property will be tolerated** 

**The People over Profit Movement**

Right now, millions of Americans across the political divide are struggling. 60% live paycheck to paycheck, many earn very low wages, and 85 million lack proper health insurance. College is too expensive for young people, a quarter of seniors live on $15,000 a year or less, and childhood poverty is among the highest in the world. We also face a severe shortage of affordable housing.

At the same time, the wealthiest Americans, like Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and Mark Zuckerberg, are getting richer. Since Trump’s election, their combined wealth has grown by over $200 billion—more than the bottom half of the country. Meanwhile, the middle class shrinks, and democracy is at risk.

Our goal is to protect democracy and create an economy that works for everyone, not just the rich. As the wealthiest country in the world, we have the potential to use new technologies to improve everyone’s lives, but instead, most of the wealth goes to the people who need it the least.

We must make healthcare a human right, raise wages to a living standard, improve public education, address the housing crisis, create good-paying jobs to fight climate change, and end all forms of discrimination.

**We the People believe that in the richest country in the history of the world we must establish that:**

1. Healthcare is a human right and must be available to all regardless of income.

2. Every worker in America is entitled to earn a decent income. We must raise the minimum wage to a living wage and make it easier for workers to join unions.

3. We must have the best public educational system in the world, from childcare to vocational training, to graduate school – available to all.

4. We must address the housing crisis and build the millions of units of low-income and affordable housing that we desperately need.

5. We must create millions of good paying jobs as we lead the world in combating the existential threat of climate change.

6. We must abolish all forms of bigotry.

**"While the constitution reserves the right to declare war to the Congress, the War Powers Act allows the president to deploy troops for 60 days without congressional approval. Trump has threatened U.S. involvement in the Iranian/Israeli conflict. We stand opposed to this threat of war and will protest against it _this Saturday_ in conjunction with our standing protest against the Trump administration attack on democracy. The location is at _6916 NE Fourth Plain Blvd from noon to 2 pm._"**

Protests at Tesla dealerships all over the country have had a huge impact on Elon Musk's company - and we've been part of it! Musk may have stepped back from DOGE, but his operatives are still wreaking havoc through the federal government. Our rallies continue to raise awareness and educate the community.

We'll march on the sidewalk/right of way outside Vancouver's Tesla showroom on Fourth Plain Blvd., staying on public property. Park on the street or in the surrounding neighborhood. Bring a large sign to let everyone know we stand united against Musk, DOGE, and unelected oligarchs!

### JUNE TIME CHANGES 
*Starting June 1, we will no longer be rallying on Wednesdays. On Saturdays we'll rally at Tesla from 12 noon - 2 pm.*

We at IGV strongly believe that peaceful, non-violent activism offers social movements the most power to effect change. Through peaceful protests, we set an example of making our voices heard with dignity, empowered by truth. IGV does not condone intimidation, threats, vandalism, interference with access to a business, or any other lawless actions. If instigators or our opponents attempt to violate our commitment to non-violence, we will try to de-escalate them and will end the event if needed to maintain a safe environment.

description:

title: Stand Up, Superior! - A Tesla/Trump Takedown
description:
Come join us on Saturdays from 11am to 2pm to peacefully protest the corruption and hatred coming from the head of our government currently. 

This will be an on-going event until the madness stops, and unfortunately, it seems as though we might be doing this for a while.
Just to be clear, signing up does not mean you are required to be at every protest. 

The sole purpose of this website is to let you know that people will be there on McCaslin Blvd. every Saturday until we are heard and changes are made.

For your mental and physical health, I recommend taking the occasional Saturday off! Know that others are there keeping the event going strong.

There may be individuals who approach on foot and try to provoke us. 
It is my hope that you’ll be able to ignore them and redirect your attention to the individuals standing beside you. 

It is a requirement of all attendees that you help uphold our commitment to non-violence and de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. 

Here are some suggestions to keep this a peaceful, civil protest: 

• Keep away from the Tesla employees, dealership, and their immediate surrounding property. Protest events at Tesla locations or other Musk properties should be focused on Elon Musk's role as a political actor and government agent. Protests should not be aimed at attacking the business interests of Tesla or their customers. 
• Stay on the sidewalk next to the public streets and keep off the lawn next to their building. 
• Stare past any agitators like they don’t exist. 
• Start a conversation about something random with someone near you. 
• Focus on music and the people driving by cheering in support. 

For your safety and the safety of those around you, consider not engaging with anyone that tries to provoke you. 

Parking and What to Bring:

• There is plenty of parking at the mall and near the Starbucks across the street from the Tesla Dealership.
• Bring a sign that expresses your feelings/what you're there for. 
• Water to stay hydrated, a sweater/coat, sunscreen, a hat, masks if you feel it necessary.
• Something to sit on if you want to attend, but cannot stand for hours on end.
• A playlist with upbeat music and a bluetooth speaker to help keep people around you positive and motivated.

“Courage is not the absence of fear, but rather the assessment that something else is more important than fear.” – Franklin D. Roosevelt 

Resist. Dissent. Persist.

description:

If You Bring a Sign, Banner, or Flag For sign and banner lettering, bigger is better, so it can be easily read from the roadway. Flags are great, too. Wouldn't it be amazing to reclaim our flag? Mass DOT does not like things attached to the fence. They may visit, so be prepared to not have anything attached. Come join like-minded folks to demand that Trump, Musk, and the Republican-led Congress stop their unconstitutional power grab and the cruel destruction of our federal government.

We will hold banners, signs, and flags, and we'll wave to passing motorists. Many will beep and wave back at us, which feels nice! We'll show people that they're not alone and help give them the courage to join us and take a stand.

Please come out whether or not you have a sign or banner or flag. More people is better!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 hour and 15 minute standout.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational and non-violent, in words and body language. 

We welcome your energy and ideas, and we're looking forward to meeting everyone. Let's have some fun and make some good trouble

title: March for Integrity (National)
description:
The [Money Out of Politics Movement](https://moneyoutofpolitics.org/) is organizing a peaceful, non-partisan mass mobilization in **Washington, D.C.**, and at **all 50 state capitals**, where we expect to mobilize at least **two million Americans** to demand:

1. A Ban on Lobbyist Gifts: Prohibiting all direct or indirect financial incentives from lobbyists to members of Congress.
2. The End of Congressional Stock Trading: Preventing elected officials from using privileged information to personally benefit.
3. The Overturning of Citizens United: Eliminating unlimited corporate campaign contributions and restoring limits on political spending.
4. A Constitutional Amendment to Keep Money Out of Politics: Ensuring that future generations do not face the same corruption and undue influence in government.

These reforms are not partisan; they are essential to ensuring a government that serves the people rather than powerful special interests.

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:

**General Visibility Rules:**

* **Distance is Key:** The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
* **"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility:** A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
* **Bridge Specifics:** Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.

**Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:**

* **Go Big:** Aim for lettering that is at least **12-24 inches tall**, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
* **Bold, Simple Fonts:** Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
* **High Contrast Colors:** This is critical!
    * **Dark letters on a light background** (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
    * **Avoid low-contrast combinations** like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
    * **Limit your color palette** to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
* **Concise Messaging:** Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
* **Material and Construction:**
    * **Sturdy materials:** Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
    * **Weatherproof:** Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
    * **Double-sided signs:** If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
* **Test Your Signs:** Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
* **Spacing (Kerning):** Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.

By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Four Corners in Lenexa  Standing Rally
description: As citizens, we can’t let the policies and actions of the Federal Government and unelected billionaires be normalized, but we can only stop what’s going on by coming together.  A STANDING RALLY  will draw attention to the situation, encouraging our neighbors to join with us. We will rally every Saturday morning from 11 AM – 12 PM.  Stay for the full hour or come by when and for how long you can. We will peacefully line the sidewalk on all four corners of 87th Parkway and Maurer Road,  holding signs on issues that are most meaningful to us or just simply standing in support of our neighbors and our country.  If sitting is more comfortable for you, you are very welcome to bring mobility or lawn chairs!! There is room for everyone!
accessibility_notes:
Here are a couple of notes on logistics.
Please be especially mindful of parking.  For example, if you live relatively nearby, please consider walking.  If you drive, there is street parking on the residential streets to the north and also a bit further on the south.  About ½ mile down on the west, there is a large civic campus garage at 17201 W 87th St. Pkwy.  In addition, on the SE, SW, and NW sides of the intersection, there are restaurants and shops with big, but commercially owned parking lots meant for customers. Note that Lenexa Point on the NW side has recently put up signs, saying they will tow non-customer cars. (Also note that if you become a customer, it’s fine to bring snacks to the rally that you have bought, but please take any empty snack containers back home with you, when you leave. In any case, no matter which direction you are coming from, if it is possible, please try to park before you reach the intersection to save on congestion and choose a spot as far away as you feel comfortable walking from, leaving closer spots to those who can’t walk as far.
The rally will start on the SE corner, but as more folks arrive, we will disperse to the SW, NW, and NE corners, as well.   If you cross from one side to another, please pay particular attention to cars turning right as you cross! 
 Participants should bring their own signs (if they want to hold them).  Note that sticks supporting the signs can’t be pointed at either end.  Also, in designing content for the signs, please remember that children will be present.  
Please stand only along the sidewalks parallel to the street and not on the grass.  However, also be sure to allow pedestrian access to the sidewalk and businesses.   We are not expecting issues, but keep in mind that a core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action.  Remember to de-escalate any potential confrontation with someone,  who disagrees with you. And of course, follow directions from our excellent Lenexa police, if asked.
We will not have speakers. The plan will simply be to hold the signs we have made and wave, if that feels right.  We expect that a lot of passing cars will honk back in approval! 
Finally, please note that all our organizers will be wearing lanyards with badges reading  “Standing Rally Corner Captain or “Standing Rally Media/City Liaison”.  If you see other folks with “Press” marked on their clothing or who are giving direction to you, know that they are not part of Four Corners and are not endorsed or vetted by us.
See you soon.  Let’s show our neighbors “what Democracy Looks Like”!!
P.S.  If you want to post an inspiring (!) story about your experience, please add #FourCornersinLenexa to your post!

title: "Moral Monday" Street Rally

address_lines: N. Main St. and W. Division St.

description:
Please join us in opposing cuts to essential safety net programs!

Please join us at recurring  "Moral Monday" street rallies in River Falls WI.

Our “Moral Monday” street rally in River Falls is on Mondays, from 4PM to 6PM, at the intersection of Main and Division Streets, where we will hold signs and stand along the public sidewalks.

Folks may join for part or all the two hours, and may bring their own signs or use signs we’ll have to share.

If the weather is bad—hard rain, high wind, and/or lightening—we’ll cancel that week’s rally.

Our "Moral Monday" street rallies are inspired and informed by work of the prominent North Carolina pastor and anti-poverty activist the Rev. William Barber, who founded the Center for Public Theology and Public Policy at Yale and now teaches there.

On the twelfth anniversary of his first "Moral Monday" demonstration, Monday April 28, 2025, Rev. Barber was arrested for praying against the Republican-led budget while in the Rotunda of our US Capitol. At a rally held before he entered the Rotunda to pray, Rev. Barber said: “Forty-three percent of women and almost half of all children are poor and low income. Somebody ought to say something … Somebody gotta challenge this budget.”

We are holding "Moral Monday" street rallies to voice our challenges.

We oppose Republican-approved Congressional budget resolutions that harm the poorest and most vulnerable of Americans in order to give more than $5-trillion in tax breaks to the richest and most privileged of Americans.

We oppose budget proposals that eliminate or make draconian cuts to federal programs for child care, health research, education, housing assistance, community development, and the elderly.

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are not just public policy choices, they are moral choices. 

These funding cuts and proposed budgets are morally wrong, not just bad public policy choices. 

Please join with us to "say something" and "challenge this budget".
